docs.title: Server Setup
docs.text: This guide covers deploying the HitStor server, including repository initialization, server startup, systemd integration, and firewall configuration.

docs.title: Create a Repository
docs.text:
Repositories can be created in two ways:

  1. From the dashboard (recommended): Navigate to Storage and click New Repository. The dashboard guides you through creating a local or S3-compatible repository.
  2. From the CLI:
hitstor init --repo /var/lib/hitstor/repo --password "REPO_PASSWORD"

For production systems, use a password file or environment variable instead of passing the password on the command line:

export HITSTOR_PASSWORD="REPO_PASSWORD"
hitstor init --repo /var/lib/hitstor/repo

docs.title: Start the Server
docs.text:
Start the HitStor server with gRPC and dashboard ports:

hitstor serve --repo /var/lib/hitstor/repo --port 8420 --dashboard-port 8421

The server opens these listeners:

Port Protocol Purpose 8420 gRPC (TLS) Agent communication -- backups, restores, scheduling 8421 HTTPS Web dashboard, JSON API and /metrics; plain HTTP requests are redirected to HTTPS (plain HTTP only while no repository exists)

The server runs in the foreground. Use systemd (see below) for production deployments.

docs.title: Repository Password
docs.text:
The server needs the repository password to decrypt and encrypt data. There are three ways to provide it:

  1. Environment variable (recommended for production):

    export HITSTOR_PASSWORD="REPO_PASSWORD"
hitstor serve --repo /var/lib/hitstor/repo

  2. Password file:

    hitstor serve --repo /var/lib/hitstor/repo --password-file /etc/hitstor/password.txt

    The file should contain the password on a single line with no trailing newline. Set permissions to 0600.

  3. Command-line flag (not recommended for production):

    hitstor serve --repo /var/lib/hitstor/repo --password "REPO_PASSWORD"

docs.title: Configuration File
docs.text:
The server reads configuration from /etc/hitstor/config.yaml when the --config flag is set. A typical server configuration:

# /etc/hitstor/config.yaml
repo: /var/lib/hitstor/repo

# TLS certificates (optional, auto-generated if omitted)
serve_tls_cert: /etc/hitstor/tls/server.crt
serve_tls_key: /etc/hitstor/tls/server.key

# Dashboard: shared password used only to create the first administrator
# (generated and logged at first start if omitted; stored as a hash)
serve_dashboard_password: "DASHBOARD_PASSWORD"

# Alerting
alert_webhook_url: "https://hooks.example.com/hitstor"
alert_stale_threshold: 25

Start the server with the config file:

hitstor serve --config /etc/hitstor/config.yaml

See Configuration for the full schema and precedence rules.

docs.title: Multi-Repository Configuration
docs.text: HitStor supports managing multiple repositories from a single server instance. This is useful for separating backups by team, environment, or retention policy.

docs.title: Defining Repositories
docs.text:
Add a repositories section to the config file:

# /etc/hitstor/config.yaml
repositories:
  - name: production
    type: local
    path: /var/lib/hitstor/prod-repo
    password_file: /etc/hitstor/prod-password

  - name: staging
    type: local
    path: /var/lib/hitstor/staging-repo
    password_file: /etc/hitstor/staging-password

  - name: offsite
    type: s3
    endpoint: s3.amazonaws.com
    bucket: company-backups
    region: us-east-1
    access_key_encrypted: <encrypted by server>
    secret_key_encrypted: <encrypted by server>
    password_file: /etc/hitstor/s3-repo-password

S3 access keys are stored encrypted (access_key_encrypted, secret_key_encrypted). Use the dashboard Storage page to create S3 repositories without editing ciphertext manually.

Each repository must have a unique name. The type field must be local or s3.

docs.title: Backward Compatibility
docs.text: If the repositories list is empty and a repo field is present, the server operates in single-repo legacy mode using the repo path and HITSTOR_PASSWORD environment variable.

docs.title: Assigning Agents to Repositories
docs.text: Each backup job targets a repository, chosen in step 2 of the New Backup Job wizard, so one agent can back up to several repositories through different jobs. The agent registry and the dashboard accounts live in the first repository (by name).

docs.title: Managing Repositories from the Dashboard
docs.text: Repositories can also be created and removed from the dashboard Storage page. See Dashboard for details.

docs.title: TLS Certificates
docs.text: All gRPC communication between server and agents is encrypted with TLS.

docs.title: Auto-Generated (Default)
docs.text:
If no --tls-cert / --tls-key flags are provided, the server automatically generates a self-signed certificate on first startup and saves it to:

  • <repo>/server.crt — certificate (distribute to agents)
  • <repo>/server.key — private key (keep on server only)

The certificate includes all of the server's IP addresses and hostname in its Subject Alternative Names (SANs), so agents can connect by IP or hostname. The certificate is reused across server restarts, and the dashboard uses it too.

Agents that have no CA certificate configured pin this certificate on their first connection, so distributing it is optional (see TLS Certificates). To distribute the certificate to agents:

scp /var/lib/hitstor/repo/server.crt agent-host:/etc/hitstor/server.crt

Then configure each agent to trust it:

# /etc/hitstor/agent-config.yaml
agent_ca_cert: /etc/hitstor/server.crt

Or via CLI flag:

hitstor-agent --ca-cert /etc/hitstor/server.crt ping

docs.title: Custom Certificates (Production)
docs.text:
For production, provide your own certificates:

hitstor serve --repo /var/lib/hitstor/repo \
  --tls-cert /etc/hitstor/tls/server.crt \
  --tls-key /etc/hitstor/tls/server.key

Or via config file:

serve_tls_cert: /etc/hitstor/tls/server.crt
serve_tls_key: /etc/hitstor/tls/server.key

If you use a certificate signed by a public CA, agents do not need the --ca-cert flag.

docs.title: Systemd Service
docs.text: On Linux systems installed via deb or rpm packages, a systemd unit is provided.

docs.title: Enable and Start
docs.text:
sudo systemctl enable hitstor-server
sudo systemctl start hitstor-server

docs.title: Environment File
docs.text:
The systemd unit reads environment variables from /etc/hitstor/server.env. Configure the repository password and any other settings here:

# /etc/hitstor/server.env
# Repository passwords are managed via the dashboard.
# For legacy single-repo mode:
# HITSTOR_PASSWORD=REPO_PASSWORD
# HITSTOR_REPO=/var/lib/hitstor/repo

Set permissions so only root can read the file:

sudo chmod 0600 /etc/hitstor/server.env
sudo chown root:root /etc/hitstor/server.env

docs.title: Check Status
docs.text:
sudo systemctl status hitstor-server
sudo journalctl -u hitstor-server -f

docs.title: Firewall Rules
docs.text:
Open the gRPC and dashboard ports on the server. For firewalld:

sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --add-port=8420/tcp
sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --add-port=8421/tcp
sudo firewall-cmd --reload

For ufw (Ubuntu/Debian):

sudo apt install ufw
sudo ufw allow 22/tcp comment "SSH"
sudo ufw allow 8420/tcp comment "HitStor gRPC"
sudo ufw allow 8421/tcp comment "HitStor Dashboard"
sudo ufw enable

Warning

Always allow SSH (port 22) before running ufw enable, or you may lose remote access to the server.

Verify the rules:

sudo ufw status verbose

If the dashboard should only be accessible from a management network, restrict port 8421 accordingly:

sudo ufw allow from 10.0.0.0/24 to any port 8421 proto tcp

docs.title: Log Output
docs.text:
HitStor uses Go's slog package for structured logging. hitstor serve writes text lines (key=value) to standard error, which systemd sends to the journal. Add --json to the ExecStart line (with systemctl edit hitstor-server) to get JSON lines that tools like jq can parse:

sudo journalctl -u hitstor-server -o cat | jq .

The server also keeps recent entries for the dashboard's Logs page, and can write a rotating log file (Settings → General).

Adjust verbosity with the --verbose flag:

Flag Level Description (none) info Operational messages (backup started, agent connected) -v info Same as the default for hitstor serve -vv debug Detailed internal state (chunk processing, pack writes)

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• TLS Certificates -- configure custom certificates for production
  • Agent Management -- register agents to connect to this server
  • Dashboard -- access the web dashboard

docs.title: Server Settings
docs.text: The Settings page (/settings, administrators only) centralizes server configuration that was previously split across environment variables, YAML files, and CLI commands. It follows the same patterns as enterprise backup consoles: grouped sections, masked secrets, test-before-save, and a restart banner when network or TLS changes require it.

docs.title: Access
docs.text: Open Administration → Settings in the dashboard sidebar, or use a deep link (/settings?tab=integrations).

docs.title: Sections
docs.text: Tab What you configure General Update checks and update URL, parallel workers, sync writes, minimum free disk reserve, retention of the Logs page (in-memory entries, optional rotating log file) Security & TLS Link to Users and access, shared dashboard password, TLS certificate upload, certificate status Network gRPC port, dashboard HTTPS port, advertise address for agents Integrations Gemini API key (Sentinel) Notifications Alert webhook, stale-agent threshold, notifier plugins Email Outgoing mail server for invitations, password-reset links and reports Plugins Workload plugin packages (.hpk) available to install on agents

docs.title: Integrations
docs.text:
Configure integrations from Settings → Integrations:

  1. Gemini API key — encrypted at rest in config.yaml; used by Ransomware Sentinel when HITSTOR_SENTINEL_API_KEY is not set
  2. Gemini model — defaults to gemini-1.5-pro (or Sentinel default when unset)

Gemini is the only integration. SaaS and cloud-provider integrations were removed before the first public release (v0.1.0) along with the workloads they served.

Open the Gemini card with Configure and use Test connection before saving. If you already have a value in an environment variable, click Import from environment to migrate it into encrypted YAML.

docs.title: Dashboard password
docs.text: People sign in with personal accounts (see Users and Access). The Dashboard password field changes the shared serve_dashboard_password, which is used only to create the first administrator, or to sign in while the server has no repository yet. A restart applies it.

docs.title: TLS certificates
docs.text:
Upload a PEM certificate and private key from Security & TLS. Files are stored under /etc/hitstor/tls/ (Linux) or %ProgramData%\HitStor\tls\ (Windows) and paths are written to serve_tls_cert and serve_tls_key in the config file.

Restart required after upload — TLS is loaded at server startup.

The status card shows source (custom, repository auto-generated, or self-signed), subject, issuer, expiry, and SANs.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text: alert_webhook_url, alert_stale_threshold (default 25 hours, 1 to 8760) and alert_notifier_plugins control webhook alerts. Test webhook sends a test event. Configure from Settings → Notifications; changes apply after a restart.

docs.title: Email
docs.text: The mail server used for account emails and reports: an internal relay, a server with user name and password, or Microsoft 365 with OAuth 2.0. See Users and Access → Email.

docs.title: Plugins
docs.text: Upload signed workload plugin packages (.hpk) here; they then appear on each agent's page under Plugins, ready to install. Agents verify each package's signature before installing it. See Plugins.

docs.title: API
docs.text: See Dashboard HTTP API — Settings.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Sentinel
  • TLS Certificates
  • Configuration Reference

docs.title: TLS Certificates
docs.text: All gRPC communication between the HitStor server and agents is encrypted with TLS, and the dashboard is served over HTTPS with the same certificate. This guide covers the default self-signed certificate behavior, custom certificate configuration, and certificate management for agents.

docs.title: Default Behavior: Self-Signed Certificates
docs.text:
When the server starts without explicit certificate configuration, it automatically generates a self-signed TLS certificate and private key. This provides encryption out of the box with no additional setup.

The auto-generated certificate is:

  • Created at the first startup and saved as server.crt and server.key in the directory of the server's first repository (for example /var/lib/hitstor/repo/server.crt), then reused on every restart
  • Valid for localhost, the server's hostname, 127.0.0.1 and the server's local IP addresses at the time it was generated
  • An ECDSA P-256 certificate valid for 10 years
  • Suitable for testing and internal networks

If the first repository is not on a local path (for example S3), the certificate is kept in memory and a new one is generated at each restart. To regenerate the saved certificate (for example after the server gets a new IP address), delete both files and restart the server; agents that pinned the old certificate must then forget it (see below).

docs.title: Custom Certificates
docs.text: For production deployments, provide your own TLS certificate and private key.

docs.title: Using CLI Flags
docs.text:
hitstor serve \
  --repo /var/lib/hitstor/repo \
  --tls-cert /etc/hitstor/tls/server.crt \
  --tls-key /etc/hitstor/tls/server.key

docs.title: Using the Config File
docs.text:
# /etc/hitstor/config.yaml
serve_tls_cert: /etc/hitstor/tls/server.crt
serve_tls_key: /etc/hitstor/tls/server.key

The certificate file should contain the full chain (server certificate followed by any intermediate certificates). The key file must be an unencrypted PEM-encoded private key.

You can also upload the certificate and key from Settings → Security & TLS in the dashboard; they are saved as server.crt and server.key in /etc/hitstor/tls/ (Linux) or %ProgramData%\HitStor\tls\ (Windows) and written to serve_tls_cert and serve_tls_key. Restart the server to use them.

docs.title: File Permissions
docs.text:
Restrict access to the private key, keeping it readable by the user the server runs as (hitstor with the packaged systemd unit):

sudo chown root:hitstor /etc/hitstor/tls/server.key
sudo chmod 0640 /etc/hitstor/tls/server.key

docs.title: Using Let's Encrypt
docs.text: HitStor does not integrate directly with Let's Encrypt or ACME. Generate certificates externally using a tool like certbot, then point HitStor at the resulting files.

docs.title: Example with Certbot
docs.text:
sudo certbot certonly --standalone -d backup.example.com

This creates certificate files at:

  • /etc/letsencrypt/live/backup.example.com/fullchain.pem
  • /etc/letsencrypt/live/backup.example.com/privkey.pem

The private key under /etc/letsencrypt is readable only by root, and the packaged server runs as the hitstor user, so copy both files to /etc/hitstor/tls/ (the deploy hook below does it on every renewal) and point HitStor at the copies:

# /etc/hitstor/config.yaml
serve_tls_cert: /etc/hitstor/tls/server.crt
serve_tls_key: /etc/hitstor/tls/server.key

docs.title: Renewal
docs.text:
Let's Encrypt certificates are valid for 90 days. After certbot renews the certificate, restart the HitStor server to load the new files:

sudo systemctl restart hitstor-server

To automate this, add a post-renewal hook:

# /etc/letsencrypt/renewal-hooks/deploy/hitstor-restart.sh
#!/bin/bash
set -e
live=/etc/letsencrypt/live/backup.example.com
install -o root -g hitstor -m 0644 "$live/fullchain.pem" /etc/hitstor/tls/server.crt
install -o root -g hitstor -m 0640 "$live/privkey.pem" /etc/hitstor/tls/server.key
systemctl restart hitstor-server

sudo mkdir -p /etc/hitstor/tls
sudo chmod +x /etc/letsencrypt/renewal-hooks/deploy/hitstor-restart.sh
sudo /etc/letsencrypt/renewal-hooks/deploy/hitstor-restart.sh   # first copy

docs.title: Certificate Renewal
docs.text:
When replacing certificate files (from any CA, not just Let's Encrypt), restart the server to load the new certificate:

sudo systemctl restart hitstor-server

The server reads certificate files at startup. Changes to certificate files on disk are not detected at runtime.

docs.title: Agent CA Certificate
docs.text: When the server uses a self-signed certificate or a certificate from a private CA, agents must be configured to trust that CA. Use the agent_ca_cert configuration key on each agent to point at the CA certificate file.

docs.title: Agent Configuration
docs.text:
In the agent config file:

# /etc/hitstor/agent-config.yaml
agent_ca_cert: /etc/hitstor/tls/ca.crt

Or via environment variable:

# /etc/hitstor/agent.env
HITSTOR_AGENT_CA_CERT=/etc/hitstor/tls/ca.crt

The CA certificate file should be the PEM-encoded certificate of the authority that signed the server's certificate. For self-signed certificates, use the server certificate itself (server.crt from the repository directory).

docs.title: Without a CA Certificate (Certificate Pinning)
docs.text:
If agent_ca_cert is not set, the agent trusts the server certificate it sees on its first connection and pins its SHA-256 fingerprint in /etc/hitstor/server-fingerprint (C:\ProgramData\HitStor\server-fingerprint on Windows). Later connections are refused if the server presents a different certificate, unless that certificate is valid for the server hostname under the system's trusted CAs, in which case the pin is updated automatically.

Run the first connection (for example hitstor-agent ping) on a trusted network. If you replace the server's self-signed certificate on purpose, delete the fingerprint file on each agent so it pins the new one.

docs.title: Distributing the CA Certificate
docs.text:
Copy the CA certificate to each agent machine:

scp /etc/hitstor/tls/ca.crt agent-host:/etc/hitstor/tls/ca.crt

Verify the agent can connect:

hitstor-agent ping

docs.title: Troubleshooting TLS
docs.text: Symptom Cause Solution certificate signed by unknown authority Agent does not trust the server CA Set agent_ca_cert on the agent peer certificate fingerprint ... does not match pinned The server certificate changed since the agent pinned it If the change was intended, delete the agent's server-fingerprint file; otherwise investigate a possible man-in-the-middle tls: bad certificate Certificate does not match hostname Ensure the certificate's SAN includes the server hostname or IP tls: private key does not match public key Mismatched cert and key files Regenerate or re-pair the certificate and key permission denied reading key file File permissions too restrictive Ensure the HitStor process user can read the key file

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Agent Management -- register agents that will connect over TLS
  • Security -- full security model including encryption and key derivation

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: This page covers common HitStor issues, their causes, and solutions. For each problem, the error message is shown as it appears in logs or terminal output.

docs.title: "Repository not found"
docs.text:
The full message is Repository not found at PATH.

Cause: The repository directory does not exist or has not been initialized with hitstor init.

Solution: Initialize the repository before starting the server or running backups:

hitstor init --repo /var/lib/hitstor/repo --password "REPO_PASSWORD"

If the directory exists but appears empty or corrupted, check that the path is correct and that the config file and the keys/ subdirectory are present (data/, index/ and snapshots/ appear after the first backup).

docs.title: "Incorrect password"
docs.text:
The underlying error is wrong password or corrupted key file.

Cause: The password provided does not match the password used when the repository was initialized.

Solution:

  1. Check the HITSTOR_PASSWORD environment variable:

    echo $HITSTOR_PASSWORD

  2. If using a password file (--password-file), verify the file contains the correct password with no trailing newline:

    wc -c /etc/hitstor/password.txt
cat -A /etc/hitstor/password.txt

  3. If using systemd, check the environment file:

    sudo cat /etc/hitstor/server.env

  4. Ensure there are no extra spaces, quotes, or escape characters in the password value.

docs.title: "repository is locked by another process"
docs.text:
Cause: Another HitStor process is currently using the repository, or a previous process terminated without releasing the lock.

Solution:

  1. Check for other running HitStor processes:

    ps aux | grep hitstor

  2. If no other process is running, the lock is stale. Run the command again with --break-lock, which removes stale locks before the operation:

    hitstor check --repo /var/lib/hitstor/repo --break-lock

  3. If using the server, ensure only one hitstor serve process runs against a given repository.

docs.title: "TLS connection error"
docs.text:
Cause: The agent cannot verify the server's TLS certificate. The most common causes are:

  1. The agent is configured with a CA certificate (--ca-cert, agent_ca_cert, HITSTOR_AGENT_CA_CERT) that did not sign the server's certificate
  2. The certificate does not include the address the agent connects to in its SANs (for example, the server got a new IP after the certificate was generated)
  3. The server certificate changed since the agent pinned it (see below)

Diagnosis: Check which IPs the certificate includes:

openssl x509 -in /var/lib/hitstor/repo/server.crt -noout -text | grep -A1 "Subject Alternative Name"

If it only lists 127.0.0.1 and localhost, the certificate does not contain the server's real IP.

Solution:

  1. Make sure the server binary is up to date (hitstor version)

  2. Delete the old certificate to force regeneration:

    rm -f /var/lib/hitstor/repo/server.crt /var/lib/hitstor/repo/server.key

  3. Restart the server — it generates a new certificate with all local IPs:

    hitstor serve --repo /var/lib/hitstor/repo ...

  4. Verify that the new certificate includes the correct IP:

    openssl x509 -in /var/lib/hitstor/repo/server.crt -noout -text | grep -A1 "Subject Alternative Name"
# Expected: IP Address:192.168.x.x in the list

  5. Copy the certificate to the agent and configure it:

    scp USER@SERVER_IP:/var/lib/hitstor/repo/server.crt /etc/hitstor/server.crt
hitstor-agent --ca-cert /etc/hitstor/server.crt ping

    Or via config:

    agent_ca_cert: /etc/hitstor/server.crt

docs.title: "peer certificate fingerprint ... does not match pinned"
docs.text:
Cause: The agent pinned the server's certificate on its first connection, and the server now presents a different one (regenerated or replaced certificate, or a reinstalled server).

Solution: If the change was intended, delete the pin on the agent and connect again: /etc/hitstor/server-fingerprint on Linux, C:\ProgramData\HitStor\server-fingerprint on Windows. Otherwise, investigate a possible man-in-the-middle. See TLS Certificates.

docs.title: "certificate signed by unknown authority"
docs.text:
Cause: The agent does not trust the TLS certificate presented by the server. This is common with self-signed certificates or private CAs.

Solution: Configure the agent to trust the server's certificate:

hitstor-agent --ca-cert /etc/hitstor/server.crt ping

Or permanently via config file:

# /etc/hitstor/agent-config.yaml
agent_ca_cert: /etc/hitstor/server.crt

For self-signed certificates (the default), copy the server's server.crt from the repo directory. See TLS Certificates for details.

docs.title: "tls: bad certificate"
docs.text:
Cause: The server's TLS certificate does not match the hostname or IP address the agent is connecting to.

Solution: Verify the certificate's SANs include the server's IP:

openssl x509 -in /var/lib/hitstor/repo/server.crt -noout -text | grep -A1 "Subject Alternative Name"

If the IP is missing, delete the cert and restart the server to regenerate it with all current IPs.

docs.title: "tls: private key does not match public key"
docs.text:
Cause: The certificate file and key file do not correspond to each other.

Solution: Verify the files match:

openssl x509 -noout -pubkey -in server.crt | openssl sha256
openssl pkey -pubout -in server.key | openssl sha256

This works for RSA and ECDSA keys (the auto-generated certificate uses ECDSA). If the checksums differ, the files are mismatched. Regenerate or re-pair them.

docs.title: "connection refused"
docs.text:
Cause: The server is not running, or a firewall is blocking the port.

Solution:

  1. Verify the server is running:

    sudo systemctl status hitstor-server

  2. Check the server is listening on the expected port:

    ss -tlnp | grep 8420

  3. Verify firewall rules allow traffic on ports 8420 and 8421:

    sudo firewall-cmd --list-ports
# or
sudo ufw status

  4. If connecting across networks, ensure there are no intermediate firewalls or security groups blocking the port.

docs.title: Agent Not Appearing in Dashboard
docs.text:
Cause: The agent was not registered, or the registration did not reach it.

Solution:

  1. Register it from Agents → + Add Agent (see Agent Management). The server must reach the agent on port 8422.

  2. Check the agent can reach the server:

    sudo sh -c 'set -a; . /etc/hitstor/agent.env; hitstor-agent ping'

  3. Verify HITSTOR_AGENT_SERVER and HITSTOR_AGENT_API_KEY in /etc/hitstor/agent.env.

  4. Check agent logs for errors:

    sudo journalctl -u hitstor-agent -n 50

  5. For a CLI-registered agent, ensure the agent name matches what was registered with hitstor serve agent add.

docs.title: Stale Agent Alerts
docs.text:
Cause: An agent has not completed a backup within the configured stale threshold (default: 25 hours).

Solution:

  1. Check the agent service is running:

    sudo systemctl status hitstor-agent

  2. Review agent logs for errors:

    sudo journalctl -u hitstor-agent --since "24 hours ago"

  3. Verify network connectivity between the agent and server.

  4. If the agent is intentionally offline (maintenance, decommissioned), remove it:

    hitstor serve agent remove AGENT_NAME

  5. Adjust the stale threshold if the backup schedule is less frequent than every 25 hours:

    # /etc/hitstor/config.yaml
alert_stale_threshold: 49  # hours

docs.title: "repository is locked for maintenance"
docs.text:
Cause: A check or prune operation is currently running on the repository. Only one maintenance operation can run at a time per repository.

Solution:

  1. Wait for the current operation to finish. Check the Storage page in the dashboard for operation progress.

  2. If the operation appears stuck, restart the server. The in-memory maintenance lock is released when the process exits.

  3. If you need to run a maintenance operation urgently, the API accepts "force": true in the body of POST /api/repos/{name}/check and POST /api/repos/{name}/prune; it aborts active backup sessions and acquires the lock. The dashboard has no button for it.

docs.title: "acquire lock: ..."
docs.text:
Cause: A race condition where another maintenance request acquired the lock between the initial check and the lock attempt.

Solution: Retry the operation after the current maintenance task completes.

docs.title: Slow Backups
docs.text:
Cause: Network bandwidth limitations, disk I/O bottlenecks, or suboptimal parallelism settings.

Solution:

  1. Check the --parallel setting. The default is suitable for most systems, but adjust based on available CPU cores and disk speed:

    hitstor-agent backup --parallel 4 /data

  2. Monitor network throughput during backup:

    # On the server
iftop -i eth0 -f "port 8420"

  3. Check disk I/O on both the agent and server:

    iostat -x 1

  4. For large initial backups, consider running the first backup on the local network rather than over a WAN link.

  5. Review the backup output for deduplication statistics. Low deduplication ratios on subsequent backups may indicate data churn.

docs.title: Verifying Repository Health
docs.text:
Run a structural check:

hitstor check --repo /var/lib/hitstor/repo --password "REPO_PASSWORD"

For a thorough check that reads and decrypts every blob:

hitstor check --repo /var/lib/hitstor/repo --password "REPO_PASSWORD" --read-data

The --read-data flag significantly increases check duration but verifies that all data can be decrypted and matches its expected checksums.

docs.title: Check Output
docs.text:
A healthy repository produces:

no errors found

If errors are found, the output lists affected pack files or snapshots. Contact support or consult the repository recovery documentation.

docs.title: Log Analysis
docs.text: HitStor uses Go's slog package for structured logging. Log entries include fields for timestamp, level, message, and contextual data. They are text lines (key=value) by default; run the server with --json (see Server Setup → Log Output) for JSON lines that the jq examples below expect. The dashboard's Logs page shows the same entries, filterable and exportable.

docs.title: Viewing Logs
docs.text:
# Follow server logs
sudo journalctl -u hitstor-server -f

# Follow agent logs
sudo journalctl -u hitstor-agent -f

docs.title: Filtering with jq
docs.text:
Parse and filter JSON logs (server started with --json):

# Show only errors
sudo journalctl -u hitstor-server -o cat | jq 'select(.level == "ERROR")'

# Show backup-related messages
sudo journalctl -u hitstor-server -o cat | jq 'select(.msg | contains("backup"))'

# Show messages for a specific agent
sudo journalctl -u hitstor-server -o cat | jq 'select(.agent == "web-server-01")'

# Count errors in the last 24 hours
sudo journalctl -u hitstor-server --since "24 hours ago" -o cat | jq 'select(.level == "ERROR")' | wc -l

docs.title: Common Log Fields
docs.text: Field Description time ISO 8601 timestamp level Log level (DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR) msg Human-readable message agent Agent name (for agent-related events) snapshot Snapshot ID (for snapshot-related events) duration Operation duration (for timed operations) bytes Data size (for transfer operations) error Error message (for error-level entries)

docs.title: Getting Help
docs.text:
If the troubleshooting steps above do not resolve the issue:

  1. Collect server and agent logs covering the time of the problem.
  2. Note the HitStor version (hitstor version).
  3. Note the operating system and version.
  4. Open an issue on the HitStor repository with the collected information.

docs.title: Users and Access
docs.text: The dashboard uses personal accounts. Each person signs in with their own user name, password and a code from an authenticator app, and only sees and changes what their role allows.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Role Can do Administrator Everything, on every agent: users, storage, settings, reports, deleting snapshots, disaster recovery. Backup operator Create, edit, schedule, run and cancel backup jobs; suspend and resume agents. Cannot restore. Restore operator Browse snapshots and restore them. Cannot change jobs. Viewer Read jobs, results and logs. Changes nothing.

Backup and restore are separate roles on purpose: a person who restores can read any data that was backed up, so give that role only to those who need it.

Every role except Administrator is given either on all agents or on a list of agents. A backup operator for web01 sees only web01, its jobs and their results; pages that span every agent (Overview, Storage, Disaster recovery, Logs) need the role on all agents. A user can hold several roles, for example backup operator on two agents and viewer on all.

docs.title: Two-step verification
docs.text:
Two-step verification is mandatory for every account. At the first sign-in each user:

  1. Installs an authenticator app (Microsoft Authenticator, Google Authenticator, 1Password, Bitwarden...).
  2. Scans the QR code the dashboard shows, or types the key under it.
  3. Enters the 6-digit code to confirm, and saves the 10 recovery codes shown next. Each recovery code signs in once when the phone is not at hand.

From then on, signing in asks for the password and then a code. A code can be used only once. Under My account a user can generate new recovery codes (the old ones stop working) or move the authenticator to a new phone.

If a user loses both the phone and the recovery codes, an administrator resets their two-step verification (Users → Manage → Reset two-step verification) and the user sets it up again at the next sign-in.

docs.title: Passwords
docs.text:
• At least 12 characters and at most 128. A phrase of several words is easy to remember and hard to guess.
  • Commonly used passwords and passwords containing the user name are refused.
  • There are no composition rules and no periodic expiry, as NIST SP 800-63B recommends; change a password when there is a reason to.
  • Passwords are stored as argon2id hashes.

Administrators never choose a user's password. With email set up, a new user receives an invitation link and chooses their password themselves. Without it, creating a user or resetting a password gives a temporary password: hand it over in person or by another channel. It works once: at the next sign-in the user chooses their own password and, for a new user, sets up the authenticator.

docs.title: Email
docs.text:
With an outgoing mail server set up under Settings → Email, the dashboard sends two kinds of account email (it also sends the scheduled reports):

  • Invitation. Creating a user with an email address sends them a link to choose their password; it works once and expires after 72 hours. Nobody, not even the administrator, ever sees a temporary password. If the email cannot be sent, the dashboard says why and shows a temporary password instead.
  • Password reset. Forgot your password? on the sign-in page takes a user name or email address and sends a link to choose a new password, valid for one hour. The page answers the same whether or not the account exists. An administrator can also send the link (or a new invitation, for a user who never signed in) from the user's page with Password → Reset.

The links are safe to lose in a mailbox: each works once, a newer link replaces older ones, and changing the password, the email address or disabling the account cancels them. A user who has set up two-step verification must also enter a code from the authenticator (or a recovery code) to choose a new password, so reading their email is not enough to take over the account. A new reset link cannot be requested for the same account within two minutes, and requests from one address are rate-limited.

The address in Dashboard address in the links starts every link; the dashboard never builds it from the request, so a forged Host header cannot redirect links elsewhere. Use the name people type to reach the dashboard, for example https://backup.example.com:8421.

Each user's address is set by an administrator, on the user's page or with hitstor serve user add --email; users see it under My account. Two users cannot share an address.

Send test sends an email with the settings in the form, before or after saving them, and shows the server's answer when it refuses.

docs.title: An internal relay
docs.text: A relay on the local network that accepts mail from known hosts needs no credentials. Choose Start from: Internal relay, enter the relay's name or address and the sender address, and allow the HitStor server's address on the relay. Connection security None sends without encryption: use it only on a network you trust. Use STARTTLS if the relay offers it; with a self-signed certificate, tick Accept any server certificate.

docs.title: Microsoft 365 (Exchange Online)
docs.text:
Exchange Online no longer accepts passwords for SMTP, so HitStor signs in as a registered app with OAuth 2.0 (client credentials) and sends as one mailbox. A shared mailbox is a good sender: it needs no license and has no password of its own.

  1. In the Microsoft Entra admin center, under App registrations → New registration, register an app for your organization only. Note its Application (client) ID and Directory (tenant) ID.
  2. Under API permissions → Add a permission → APIs my organization uses → Office 365 Exchange Online → Application permissions, add SMTP.SendAsApp, then Grant admin consent.
  3. Under Certificates & secrets, create a client secret and copy its value (it is shown once). Note when it expires and renew it before.

  4. In Exchange Online PowerShell, register the app's service principal and let it use the sender mailbox. The object ID is the one of the app under Enterprise applications, not under App registrations:

    Connect-ExchangeOnline
New-ServicePrincipal -AppId <client-id> -ObjectId <enterprise-app-object-id> -DisplayName "HitStor"
Add-MailboxPermission -Identity hitstor@example.com -User <enterprise-app-object-id> -AccessRights FullAccess
# Only if SMTP AUTH is turned off for the organization or the mailbox:
Set-CASMailbox -Identity hitstor@example.com -SmtpClientAuthenticationDisabled $false

  5. In HitStor, choose Start from: Microsoft 365 (smtp.office365.com, port 587, STARTTLS), enter the tenant ID, client ID and secret, the mailbox as sender address, and send a test.

The server needs to reach login.microsoftonline.com:443 (for the token) and smtp.office365.com:587. An error starting with AADSTS comes from Microsoft Entra (wrong tenant, client ID or secret, or an expired secret); 535 5.7.3 means Exchange refused the app for that mailbox (step 4).

docs.title: Sessions and lockout
docs.text:
• A session ends after 30 minutes without activity (15 for administrators) and after 12 hours in any case. Only what the user does counts as activity: opening pages, typing, clicking. Automatic refreshes do not, so a page left open on an unattended computer still times out. Two minutes before, the dashboard warns and offers to stay signed in.
  • Deleting users, changing roles, resetting passwords, deleting snapshots, pruning, recovering a server and similar changes ask for the password and a code again if the last sign-in was more than 15 minutes ago.
  • After 10 wrong passwords or codes an account is locked for 15 minutes. Repeated failures from one address are also slowed down.
  • My account lists the user's open sessions and can end any of them. Administrators can end anybody's sessions under Users.

docs.title: The first administrator
docs.text:
When a server is upgraded from a version with a single dashboard password, the dashboard opens at Create the first administrator. Enter the current dashboard password (from serve_dashboard_password, or the one printed in the server log) and choose the administrator's user name and password. Then set up the authenticator. From that moment the shared password no longer signs in.

Accounts are stored next to the agent registry in the first repository (by name, in alphabetical order), in users.json, encrypted with the repository key. Until the server has a repository, the dashboard still signs in with the shared password.

docs.title: Managing users
docs.text:
Administrators manage accounts under Users and access. The list can be searched and filtered by role and status; a row opens the user's page:

  • Roles and agents: each role with its explanation, on all agents or on some. In short says in plain words what the user can do.
  • Sessions: where the user is signed in; any session can be ended.
  • Activity: the user's latest entries in the audit log.
  • Account: full name, status, and resetting the password or two-step verification.
  • Danger zone: disabling the user, or removing them after typing their user name.

The last active administrator cannot be removed, disabled or lose the role.

docs.title: From the server console
docs.text:
hitstor serve user manages accounts directly on the server, for example when no administrator can sign in. Run it with the same configuration and repository password as the service; changes apply to a running server immediately.

# Create an administrator; prints a temporary password
hitstor serve user add maria --grant admin --display-name "Maria Perez" --email maria@example.com

# A backup operator for two agents who can also read everything
hitstor serve user add ops1 --grant backup_operator=web01,db01 --grant viewer

hitstor serve user list
hitstor serve user grant ops1 --grant restore_operator=db01   # replaces the roles
hitstor serve user passwd maria        # new temporary password, ends sessions
hitstor serve user reset-2fa maria     # set up the authenticator again
hitstor serve user disable ops1
hitstor serve user enable ops1         # also lifts a lockout
hitstor serve user remove ops1

docs.title: Audit log
docs.text: Audit log (administrators) lists sign-ins, failed attempts, changes to users, backups, restores, storage and settings, and denied requests, with user, address and time, in plain sentences. It can be filtered by user, type of action, result and period, and exported to CSV. Each entry carries the hash of the previous one, so editing or deleting an entry breaks the chain, and the page says where. The log is audit.log, next to users.json; changes made with hitstor serve user appear as user console.

docs.title: HitStor Visual Branding
docs.text: Design system for the HitStor web dashboard and login experience. The goal is a cohesive, professional identity: navy depth + orange energy + clean light surfaces.

docs.title: Brand essence
docs.text:
• Trust & security — deep navy backgrounds, padlock isotipo, restrained typography
  • Action & warmth — orange accents on primary actions, active nav, and the stor wordmark syllable
  • Clarity — light content areas, white cards, generous spacing

docs.title: Color palette
docs.text: Token Hex / value Usage --brand-navy-deep #071018 Gradient start --navy #0b1f3a Gradient mid, headings on light cards --brand-navy-light #132d4f Gradient end --brand-text #f4f7fb Text on navy surfaces --brand-text-muted rgba(244,247,251,0.75) Secondary text on navy --brand-accent #ff7a45 stor syllable, version pill, nav active bar --primary #e8602c Buttons, metrics, bullet dots --primary-dark #cf4f1f Button hover --content-gradient #f8fafc → #f1f5f9 Login right panel, dashboard content background

docs.title: Gradients
docs.text:
Navy brand surface (header, sidebar, login left panel):

--brand-gradient: linear-gradient(145deg, #071018 0%, #0b1f3a 42%, #132d4f 100%);

Ambient glow overlay (always paired with navy surfaces):

--brand-glow: radial-gradient(circle at 20% 20%, rgba(232,96,44,0.18), transparent 42%),
              radial-gradient(circle at 80% 70%, rgba(255,255,255,0.06), transparent 35%);

docs.title: Isotipo (assets/icon.svg → internal/dashboard/static/icon.svg)
docs.text:
• Padlock whose body continues into stacked backup layers, orange on a navy rounded tile (64-unit grid)
  • The SVG carries its own tile, radius and hairline rim, so CSS adds no border-radius; use filter: drop-shadow on navy backgrounds
  • favicon.svg is a simplified cut (no keyhole, one layer) that stays legible at 16px
  • Next to the wordmark, use the horizontal lockup: the icon is 1em tall and centred on the letters (.brand-lockup)

docs.title: Wordmark (HTML, not an image)
docs.text:
<span class="brand-wordmark">
  <span class="wm-hit">hit</span><span class="wm-stor">stor</span>
</span>
Syllable Color Weight hit --brand-text (white on navy) 800 stor --brand-accent (orange) 800

Letter-spacing: -0.04em. Prefer the HTML wordmark over logo.png in the dashboard shell for crisp rendering at any DPI.

docs.title: When to use which asset
docs.text: Context Asset Dashboard header Isotipo + HTML wordmark (once; not repeated in sidebar) Login hero panel Horizontal lockup (.brand-lockup): isotipo + wordmark README / external docs logo.svg / logo-dark.svg (isotipo + wordmark lockup) Favicon favicon.svg (PNG fallback favicon.png)

docs.title: Typography
docs.text:
• UI: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif
  • Monospace (repo IDs, codes): SF Mono, Cascadia Code, Fira Code
  • Wordmark sizes: 3.25rem (login hero), 1.35rem (sidebar), 1.15rem (header)

docs.title: Layout shell (authenticated dashboard)
docs.text:
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Navy header — isotipo + wordmark · repo id · version   │
├──────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Navy    │  Light gradient content area                 │
│  sidebar │  White cards, orange metric accents          │
│  (nav)   │                                              │
└──────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  • Header: full-width navy gradient with glow; sticky top; single brand placement (isotipo + wordmark)
  • Sidebar: same navy gradient, navigation only; active item has orange left border

docs.title: Dev Guide
docs.text: The HitStor Dev Guide is an internal reference for building, packaging, testing, and releasing HitStor. It also covers preparing a fresh Ubuntu server to receive a HitStor installation.

docs.title: Topics
docs.text: Guide Description Codebase Overview Architecture map, binaries, packages, and feature maturity. Plugin Architecture Design of installable workload plugins (SQL Server first). Dev Environment Install all prerequisite tools needed to build and package HitStor. Build & Packaging Compile binaries and produce .deb, .rpm, Windows, and Docker packages. Server Preparation Prepare an Ubuntu server before installing the HitStor .deb package. Testing Run unit tests, integration tests, linting, and code coverage. Benchmarks Reproducible backup/restore timings (optional restic comparison). Release Process Cut a release, generate all artifacts, and publish to GitHub.

docs.title: Performance benchmarks
docs.text:
HitStor ships a reproducible filesystem backup/restore harness under benchmarks/.

Use it to:

  • Compare releases (same machine, same profile)
  • Produce optional restic side-by-side numbers
  • Support published claims with raw JSON + methodology

Full detail: benchmarks/README.md in the repository.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
# From repository root
./benchmarks/run.sh --profile small

# Or via Make
make bench
make bench PROFILE=medium

Outputs: results.md and results.json in the work directory printed at the end of the run.

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text: Profile Intent tiny Script smoke (~seconds) small Default laptop lab (~100 MiB logical) medium Publishable lab run (~1 GiB logical) large Server-class stress (~5 GiB logical)

docs.title: What “good” looks like for product messaging
docs.text:
This harness measures filesystem backup, the core of HitStor (Roadmap), so quote numbers that matter to filesystem buyers:

  1. Full backup MiB/s on local disk
  2. Incremental wall time after small change set
  3. Restore MiB/s (trust + RTO)
  4. On-disk repo size vs source (dedup effectiveness)

Always pair throughput with hardware class (CPU, RAM, NVMe vs HDD).

docs.title: Latest lab run
docs.text:
A format example (profile tiny, not for marketing) lives at benchmarks/results/sample-tiny.md.

Replace this section with a medium/large run on representative hardware:

./benchmarks/run.sh --profile medium --workdir /var/tmp/hitstor-bench
# paste results.md table below; archive results.json with the release
Tool Full backup Incremental Restore Repo size (MiB) Full MiB/s Restore MiB/s pending (publish medium/large run) — — — — — —

See also: restore verification (hitstor verify-restore) for correctness after restore.

docs.title: Build & Packaging
docs.text: This page documents every Makefile target for compiling binaries and producing distributable packages. All packaging-related configuration lives under the packaging/ directory.

docs.title: Server
docs.text:
make build                  # bin/hitstor        (linux/amd64)
make build-arm64            # bin/hitstor-arm64   (linux/arm64)
make build-windows          # bin/hitstor.exe     (windows/amd64)

docs.title: Agent
docs.text:
make agent                  # bin/hitstor-agent           (linux/amd64)
make agent-arm64            # bin/hitstor-agent-arm64      (linux/arm64)
make agent-windows          # bin/hitstor-agent.exe        (windows/amd64)
make agent-windows-arm64    # bin/hitstor-agent-arm64.exe  (windows/arm64)

docs.title: All Binaries
docs.text:
make build-all

Builds all server and agent binaries for every platform in a single command.

docs.title: Plugins
docs.text:
make plugins

Builds all four plugin binaries to bin/:

Target Output make plugin-memory bin/hitstor-backend-memory make notifier-log bin/hitstor-notifier-log make hook-log bin/hitstor-hook-log make scanner-builtin bin/hitstor-scanner-builtin

These are the built-in plugin types (storage, notifier, hook, scanner). Workload plugins such as SQL Server are packaged separately; see below.

docs.title: Workload Plugin Packages (.hpk)
docs.text:
Workload plugins live under plugins/<id>/ and ship as signed .hpk packages (see Workload Plugin Architecture).

make pluginkit                          # bin/hitstor-pluginkit
make plugin-packages PLUGIN_UNSIGNED=1  # unsigned packages, for local development
make plugin-packages PLUGIN_KEY_FILE=mykey.key

make plugin-packages builds each entry of WORKLOAD_PLUGIN_TARGETS (by default example:linux/amd64 example:windows/amd64 mssql:windows/amd64) into bin/plugins/ and packs it with hitstor-pluginkit pack into dist/hitstor-plugin-<id>-<version>-<os>-<arch>.hpk. The package version comes from the plugin's plugins/<id>/plugin.yaml, not from VERSION.

The signing key (a base64 ed25519 seed) is read from PLUGIN_KEY_FILE, or else from the HITSTOR_PLUGIN_SIGNING_KEY environment variable, which is how the release workflow signs. Agents reject unsigned packages unless plugin_allow_unsigned is set, and accept only packages signed with the official key embedded in the agent or a key listed in plugin_trusted_keys. To sign in-house plugins, create a key pair and check a package:

bin/hitstor-pluginkit keygen --out mykey
bin/hitstor-pluginkit verify dist/hitstor-plugin-example-0.1.0-windows-amd64.hpk

docs.title: Protobuf Code Generation
docs.text:
Regenerate .pb.go and _grpc.pb.go files after modifying .proto definitions:

make proto            # All protos (backup + agent + plugin)
make proto-backup     # internal/proto/hitstor/v1/backup.proto only
make proto-agent      # internal/proto/hitstor/v1/agent.proto only
make proto-plugin     # api/proto/hitstor/plugin/v1/*.proto only

Note

Plugin protos require the -I api/proto include path for cross-file imports. This is already configured in the Makefile.

docs.title: Linux Packages (.deb / .rpm)
docs.text: Linux packages are built with nfpm using YAML configuration files in packaging/nfpm/.

docs.title: Makefile Targets
docs.text:
Target Prerequisite Output make pkg-server-deb bin/hitstor dist/hitstor_VERSION_amd64.deb make pkg-server-rpm bin/hitstor dist/hitstor-VERSION-1.x86_64.rpm make pkg-agent-deb bin/hitstor-agent, bin/hitstor-scanner-builtin dist/hitstor-agent_VERSION_amd64.deb make pkg-agent-rpm bin/hitstor-agent, bin/hitstor-scanner-builtin dist/hitstor-agent-VERSION-1.x86_64.rpm make pkg-linux (all above) All 4 Linux packages

Each target automatically builds its prerequisite binaries first.

docs.title: Setting the Version
docs.text:
Pass the VERSION variable to control the package version:

make pkg-server-deb VERSION=1.2.0

If not specified, VERSION defaults to dev.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text: nfpm reads a YAML config (e.g. packaging/nfpm/hitstor-server.yaml), takes the pre-built binary from bin/, and bundles it together with systemd units, configuration examples, and install scripts into a .deb or .rpm.

docs.title: Server Package Contents
docs.text:
Source Installed To Description bin/hitstor /usr/bin/hitstor Server binary packaging/scripts/grant-hitstor-journal-access.sh /usr/lib/hitstor/grant-journal-access.sh Lets the hitstor user read the journal (dashboard Logs page) packaging/systemd/hitstor-server.service /usr/lib/systemd/system/hitstor-server.service systemd unit packaging/systemd/hitstor-server.env.example /etc/hitstor/server.env.example Environment file template packaging/config/server-config.yaml.example /etc/hitstor/config.yaml.example Configuration template

Post-install script (packaging/scripts/server-postinstall.sh):

  • Creates hitstor system user and group
  • Adds the hitstor user to the systemd-journal group (through grant-journal-access.sh)
  • Creates /var/lib/hitstor, /var/log/hitstor, /etc/hitstor, /usr/lib/hitstor/plugins
  • Copies server.env.example to server.env and config.yaml.example to config.yaml (mode 600) if they do not exist
  • Runs systemctl daemon-reload

docs.title: Agent Package Contents
docs.text:
Source Installed To Description bin/hitstor-agent /usr/bin/hitstor-agent Agent binary bin/hitstor-scanner-builtin /usr/lib/hitstor/plugins/hitstor-scanner-builtin Built-in filesystem scanner plugin packaging/systemd/hitstor-agent.service /usr/lib/systemd/system/hitstor-agent.service systemd unit packaging/systemd/hitstor-agent.env.example /etc/hitstor/agent.env.example Environment file template packaging/config/agent-config.yaml.example /etc/hitstor/agent-config.yaml.example Configuration template (directory) /usr/share/hitstor/bmr, /var/lib/hitstor/bmr Bare-metal recovery hook and media (/var/lib/hitstor/bmr is root-only) (directory) /var/lib/hitstor/plugins Installed workload plugin packages (root-only)

Post-install script (packaging/scripts/agent-postinstall.sh):

  • Creates /etc/hitstor and /usr/lib/hitstor/plugins
  • Copies agent.env.example to agent.env and agent-config.yaml.example to agent-config.yaml (mode 600) if they do not exist
  • Runs systemctl daemon-reload

The agent package ships no systemd timer: the server schedules backups. The postinstall script disables a hitstor-agent.timer left by versions before 0.2.1.

docs.title: nfpm Configuration Files
docs.text:
• packaging/nfpm/hitstor-server.yaml — server package definition
  • packaging/nfpm/hitstor-agent.yaml — agent package definition

Both use ${VERSION} and ${ARCH} environment variables, which are set by the Makefile at build time.

docs.title: Self-Extracting Installers (.run)
docs.text: Self-extracting .run installers bundle the binary, systemd units, configuration templates, and an interactive wizard into a single executable shell archive. The user downloads one file, runs it with sudo, and the wizard configures the essentials (data directory, dashboard password and ports for the server; the listen port for the agent), then enables and starts the service. Repositories are created afterwards from the dashboard.

docs.title: Makefile Targets
docs.text:
Target Prerequisite Output make installer-server bin/hitstor dist/hitstor-server-VERSION-linux-amd64.run make installer-server-arm64 bin/hitstor-arm64 dist/hitstor-server-VERSION-linux-arm64.run make installer-agent bin/hitstor-agent dist/hitstor-agent-VERSION-linux-amd64.run make installer-agent-arm64 bin/hitstor-agent-arm64 dist/hitstor-agent-VERSION-linux-arm64.run make installers (server + agent amd64) Both amd64 installers 
make installer-server VERSION=1.2.0
make installer-agent VERSION=1.2.0

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
The build script (packaging/installer/build-installer.sh) assembles a .run file in four steps:

  1. Collect payload — copies the binary, systemd units, and config examples into a temp directory
  2. Create archive — compresses the payload into a tar.gz
  3. Inline libraries — replaces __INLINE_*__ markers in the .sh.in template with the contents of the corresponding lib/*.sh files
  4. Assemble — substitutes __VERSION__, then concatenates the assembled shell header and the tar.gz payload into a single file

The resulting .run file has this structure:

┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│ Shell script header             │  ← Installer logic (v2 template
│ (with inlined library code)     │     + all libraries inlined)
├─────────────────────────────────┤
│ __PAYLOAD_BELOW__               │  ← Marker line
├─────────────────────────────────┤
│ tar.gz binary payload           │  ← Binary + configs + service files
└─────────────────────────────────┘

At runtime, the shell header finds the __PAYLOAD_BELOW__ marker, extracts the tar.gz from that offset into a temp directory, and runs the installation steps.

docs.title: Installer Source Files
docs.text:
The v2 installer uses a modular architecture with shared libraries inlined at build time:

File Description packaging/installer/build-installer.sh Build script that assembles the .run file packaging/installer/server-installer-v2.sh.in Shell header template for the server installer packaging/installer/agent-installer-v2.sh.in Shell header template for the agent installer

Shared libraries in packaging/installer/lib/:

File __INLINE_*__ Marker Description lib/common.sh __INLINE_COMMON__ Flag parsing, color output, payload extraction, banner, root/systemd checks lib/wizard-server.sh __INLINE_WIZARD_SERVER__ Interactive server wizard (data directory, dashboard password, gRPC and dashboard ports, advertise address) lib/wizard-agent.sh __INLINE_WIZARD_AGENT__ Interactive agent wizard (listen port; the agent is then added from the dashboard) lib/verify.sh __INLINE_VERIFY__ Post-install verification (port listening, service status) lib/uninstall.sh __INLINE_UNINSTALL__ Clean removal of binaries, service files, config, data lib/upgrade.sh __INLINE_UPGRADE__ In-place upgrade with automatic rollback on failure

docs.title: Installer Flags
docs.text:
Both server and agent installers accept the same flags:

Flag Description --no-wizard Skip the interactive wizard (reads config from environment variables) --uninstall Remove all installed files, stop and disable services --yes Skip confirmation prompts (with --uninstall) --version Print installer version and exit --help, -h Show usage information

docs.title: Installer Behavior
docs.text:
The installer auto-detects the installation mode:

  1. Fresh install — if no existing binary is found, runs the interactive wizard (or --no-wizard for automation)
  2. Upgrade — if an existing binary is found at /usr/bin/hitstor or /usr/bin/hitstor-agent, runs the upgrade flow automatically
  3. Uninstall — when --uninstall is passed, removes everything (with confirmation prompt)

docs.title: Fresh Install (Wizard)
docs.text: The wizard prompts for the configuration, writes the config files, enables and starts the service, then verifies the ports are listening. It does not create a repository: the server starts without one and the dashboard offers to create or connect one.

docs.title: Fresh Install (--no-wizard)
docs.text:
For automated deployments, pass configuration via environment variables:

# Server (all optional; defaults shown)
sudo HITSTOR_DATA_DIR=/var/lib/hitstor \
     HITSTOR_GRPC_PORT=8420 \
     HITSTOR_DASHBOARD_PORT=8421 \
     HITSTOR_ADVERTISE_ADDR=backup.example.com:8420 \
     HITSTOR_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD='choose-a-password' \
     ./hitstor-server-1.0.0-linux-amd64.run --no-wizard

# Agent (default listen port 8422)
sudo HITSTOR_AGENT_LISTEN_PORT=8422 \
     ./hitstor-agent-1.0.0-linux-amd64.run --no-wizard

HITSTOR_ADVERTISE_ADDR defaults to the detected outbound IP and the gRPC port. Without HITSTOR_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD, the server generates a dashboard password at first start and prints it once in the log; it is used to create the first administrator. The agent is then added from the dashboard with its address and token (hitstor-agent show-id).

docs.title: Upgrade with Rollback
docs.text:
When the installer detects an existing installation:

  1. Backs up the current binary (to /usr/bin/hitstor.rollback or /usr/bin/hitstor-agent.rollback)
  2. Stops the service
  3. Replaces the binary with the new version
  4. Starts the service
  5. Verifies the service is running
  6. On failure: automatically restores the backup binary and restarts the old version

Configuration files are never overwritten — user edits are always preserved. Example files are updated to the latest version.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
sudo ./hitstor-server-1.0.0-linux-amd64.run --uninstall

Stops and disables the service, removes the binary, systemd units, and optionally removes configuration and data directories (with confirmation).

docs.title: Server Installer Payload
docs.text:
File in Archive Installed To hitstor /usr/bin/hitstor hitstor-server.service /usr/lib/systemd/system/hitstor-server.service config.yaml.example /etc/hitstor/config.yaml.example server.env.example /etc/hitstor/server.env.example

/etc/hitstor/config.yaml (ports, advertise address, dashboard password) and /etc/hitstor/server.env are written from the wizard answers. The server installer also creates the hitstor system user/group and the /var/lib/hitstor and /var/log/hitstor directories.

docs.title: Agent Installer Payload
docs.text:
File in Archive Installed To hitstor-agent /usr/bin/hitstor-agent hitstor-agent.service /usr/lib/systemd/system/hitstor-agent.service agent-config.yaml.example /etc/hitstor/agent-config.yaml.example + /etc/hitstor/agent-config.yaml agent.env.example /etc/hitstor/agent.env.example

/etc/hitstor/agent.env is written with HITSTOR_AGENT_LISTEN_PORT; if it already holds a registration (HITSTOR_AGENT_SERVER), only the listen port is updated.

docs.title: Windows Packages (.exe Installers)
docs.text:
Windows installers are built with NSIS using scripts in packaging/nsis/.

Target Prerequisite Output make pkg-server-windows bin/hitstor.exe dist/hitstor-VERSION-windows-amd64-setup.exe make pkg-agent-windows bin/hitstor-agent.exe dist/hitstor-agent-VERSION-windows-amd64-setup.exe make pkg-windows (both above) Both Windows installers

Both targets first run make render-windows-icon, which regenerates packaging/nsis/hitstor.ico from assets/icon.png (needs Python with Pillow).

docs.title: NSIS Scripts
docs.text:
• packaging/nsis/hitstor-server.nsi — server installer (installs to %PROGRAMFILES%\HitStor, adds to PATH, optional firewall rules and Windows Service registration; supports /S)
  • packaging/nsis/hitstor-agent.nsi — agent installer (installs to %PROGRAMFILES%\HitStor Agent, optional Windows Service registration)

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
make docker-build VERSION=1.2.0

Uses the multi-stage Dockerfile at the project root:

  1. Builder stage — golang:1.26-alpine, compiles the server binary
  2. Runtime stage — alpine:3.22, copies the binary, exposes ports 8420 (gRPC) and 8421 (dashboard)

docs.title: Save for Distribution
docs.text:
make docker-save VERSION=1.2.0

Produces dist/hitstor-VERSION-docker.tar.gz, a gzipped tarball that can be loaded with docker load.

docs.title: Quickstart Stack
docs.text:
make docker-quickstart-up     # needs .env (copy .env.example and set HITSTOR_PASSWORD)
make docker-quickstart-down

These wrap docker compose -f docker-compose.quickstart.yml. Published images are built by .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml, not by these targets.

docs.title: Releases
docs.text: Pushing a vX.Y.Z tag builds every release asset in CI and publishes the GitHub release. See Release Process.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
make docs-serve     # Local preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000/hitstor/
make docs-build     # Build to site/ (with --strict)
make docs-deploy    # Deploy to GitHub Pages

docs.title: Output Directory
docs.text:
All distributable artifacts are written to dist/. This directory is created automatically by the packaging targets and cleaned by:

make clean          # Removes bin/, dist/, and site/

docs.title: Codebase Overview
docs.text: This guide maps the HitStor repository for developers joining the project or updating documentation. It reflects the current tree, not historical README content.

docs.title: What HitStor Is
docs.text:
HitStor is an encrypted, deduplicated backup platform written in Go (CGO_ENABLED=0). It supports:

  • Local CLI backups — hitstor backup against a local, S3, or plugin repository
  • Centralized server/agent backups — thick-agent design over gRPC/TLS
  • Bare-metal restore — ReaR-based recovery media for Linux hosts
  • Embedded dashboard — monitoring, scheduling, restore, user accounts with roles and two-step verification, email notifications, and scheduled PDF reports

The core backs up filesystems (Windows and Linux); applications are backed up through installable workload plugins (plugins/, see Workload Plugin Architecture), starting with SQL Server. M365, Google Workspace, the built-in database integrations, and cloud-VM/VMware backup were removed before the first public release (v0.1.0) — see Roadmap.

docs.title: Directory Layout
docs.text:
cmd/                          # Binaries (entry points)
  hitstor/                    # Main CLI + hitstor serve
  hitstor-agent/              # Remote backup agent
  hitstor-backend-memory/     # Example storage plugin
  hitstor-notifier-log/       # Example notifier plugin
  hitstor-hook-log/           # Example hook plugin
  hitstor-scanner-builtin/    # Built-in filesystem scanner plugin (ships with core agent)
  hitstor-pluginkit/          # Builds, signs, and verifies workload plugin packages (.hpk)

plugins/                      # Workload plugins, one directory each (packaged as .hpk)
  example/                    # Reference workload plugin
  mssql/                      # SQL Server plugin (VDI; Windows only)

internal/                     # Core libraries (not importable externally)
  archiver/                   # Local backup pipeline
  restorer/                   # Restore pipeline
  repository/                 # Content-addressable store
  server/                     # gRPC BackupService, sessions, multi-repo
  agent/                      # Remote backup client + AgentService
  dashboard/                  # Embedded web UI + HTTP API
  discovery/                  # LAN agent auto-discovery
  bmr/                        # Bare-metal restore (ReaR recovery media)
  sentinel/                   # Ransomware telemetry + Gemini analysis
  config/                     # YAML config + multi-repo repositories[]
  plugin/                     # HashiCorp go-plugin manager
  pluginpkg/                  # Plugin package format, signing, and trust
  pluginmgr/                  # Agent plugin store: install, upgrade, remove
  users/                      # Dashboard accounts, roles, two-step verification
  mailer/                     # Outgoing email (SMTP relay, user/password, Microsoft 365 OAuth)
  report/                     # PDF reports
  runlog/                     # History of backup runs (for reports)
  retention/                  # Retention policies, incl. workload backup chains
  ...                         # chunker, crypto, cron, metrics, etc.

api/proto/hitstor/plugin/v1/  # Public plugin gRPC definitions
internal/proto/hitstor/v1/    # Server/agent backup protos (backup.proto, agent.proto)

packaging/                    # systemd, nfpm, NSIS, installers
docs/                         # MkDocs site (this documentation)
specs/                        # Feature specs (local only — gitignored, not part of the published repo)

docs.title: Binaries
docs.text:
Output Makefile target Role bin/hitstor make build CLI + serve bin/hitstor-agent make agent Remote agent bin/hitstor-backend-memory make plugin-memory Storage plugin example bin/hitstor-notifier-log make notifier-log Notifier plugin example bin/hitstor-hook-log make hook-log Hook plugin example bin/hitstor-scanner-builtin make scanner-builtin Built-in FS scanner plugin (ships with agent) bin/hitstor-pluginkit make pluginkit Builds, signs, and verifies .hpk packages dist/hitstor-plugin-<id>-<version>-<os>-<arch>.hpk make plugin-packages Workload plugin packages (plugins/*)

Build all plugins: make plugins

docs.title: Runtime Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph serverBox [hitstor serve]
        GRPC[gRPC :8420 BackupService]
        HTTP[HTTP :8421 Dashboard]
        GRPC --> Repo[(Repository)]
    end

    Agent[hitstor-agent daemon] -->|upload chunks| GRPC
    HTTP -->|WakeUp browse configure| AgentSvc[AgentService :8422]
    AgentSvc --- Agent

    CLI[hitstor backup] --> Repo

docs.title: Local backup flow
docs.text: hitstor backup → scan (internal/fs or scanner plugin) → FastCDC → dedup (session + SQLite cache + index) → encrypt → pack → snapshot.

docs.title: Agent backup flow
docs.text: Agent scans/chunks/compresses locally → CheckBlobs / UploadChunks over gRPC → server encrypts, packs, snapshots. Incremental detection uses previous snapshot metadata from BeginSession (no agent-side SQLite).

docs.title: Feature Maturity
docs.text:
Feature Status Notes Filesystem backup (CLI + agent) Stable Core engine Remote server + dashboard Stable gRPC + HTTP Backup jobs + scheduling Stable Cron (incl. L, D#N, DL), interval, timezone; job_type is files or workload Workload plugins Available Signed .hpk packages; SQL Server (VDI) full, differential, and log backups as a per-kind backup plan, with per-database results and point-in-time restore Users, roles, two-step verification Available Personal dashboard accounts, per-agent roles, mandatory TOTP, audit log Email and PDF reports Available SMTP or Microsoft 365 (OAuth 2.0); scheduled PDF reports Bare-metal restore Available (Linux) ReaR-based recovery media; Windows comes later — see Roadmap Agent auto-discovery Stable Dashboard + /api/discover/* Ransomware Sentinel Stable Optional; Gemini via Settings or HITSTOR_SENTINEL_API_KEY

M365, Google Workspace, database, and cloud-VM/VMware backup — along with the workload collector plugin type that served them — were permanently removed before the first public release (v0.1.0). See Roadmap.

Topic File Config keys internal/config/config.go (Config, RepoConfig) and internal/config/config_registry.go (Registry) Dashboard HTTP routes internal/dashboard/dashboard.go (Handler() mux) Backup gRPC internal/proto/hitstor/v1/backup.proto Agent management gRPC internal/proto/hitstor/v1/agent.proto Plugin APIs api/proto/hitstor/plugin/v1/*.proto Makefile targets Makefile

docs.title: Dev Environment Setup
docs.text: This page lists every tool required to build, package, test, and document HitStor from source.

docs.title: Go Toolchain
docs.text:
HitStor requires Go 1.26.10 or later.

go version
go version go1.26.10 linux/amd64

Set up your PATH and GOPATH so that binaries installed with go install are available:

export GOPATH="$HOME/gopath"
export PATH="$GOPATH/bin:$(go env GOROOT)/bin:$PATH"

Tip

Add these exports to your ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc so they persist across sessions.

docs.title: Protobuf Compiler
docs.text: Required only when modifying .proto files (gRPC protocol or plugin interfaces).

docs.title: protoc
docs.text:
Install the Protocol Buffers compiler:

sudo apt install -y protobuf-compiler
protoc --version
libprotoc 3.21.12

docs.title: Go Plugins
docs.text:
go install google.golang.org/protobuf/cmd/protoc-gen-go@latest
go install google.golang.org/grpc/cmd/protoc-gen-go-grpc@latest

The checked-in .pb.go files were generated with protoc 3.21.12, protoc-gen-go v1.36.11 and protoc-gen-go-grpc v1.6.2 (see the header of each generated file); use the same versions to keep regeneration diffs small.

Verify both are on your PATH:

which protoc-gen-go
/home/user/gopath/bin/protoc-gen-go

which protoc-gen-go-grpc
/home/user/gopath/bin/protoc-gen-go-grpc

docs.title: nfpm (Linux Packages)
docs.text:
nfpm builds .deb and .rpm packages from YAML configuration files.

go install github.com/goreleaser/nfpm/v2/cmd/nfpm@v2.44.0
nfpm --version

The release workflow pins nfpm v2.44.0.

Warning

go install places the binary in $GOPATH/bin, not $(go env GOROOT)/bin. Make sure $GOPATH/bin is on your PATH.

docs.title: NSIS / makensis (Windows Packages)
docs.text:
Required only when building Windows .exe installers.

sudo apt install -y nsis python3-pil
makensis -VERSION

The Windows targets first run make render-windows-icon (scripts/render-windows-icon.sh), which uses Python with Pillow (python3-pil) to generate packaging/nsis/hitstor.ico from assets/icon.png.

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
Required only when building container images.

Install Docker Engine following the official documentation.

docker --version

docs.title: Documentation Tools
docs.text:
MkDocs with the Material theme generates the documentation site.

pip install -r requirements-docs.txt
mkdocs --version

requirements-docs.txt pins MkDocs, Material, and mkdocs-static-i18n (the English/Spanish site). Material brings the Markdown extensions the site uses (admonitions, tabbed, superfences, etc.).
