docs.title: Testing
docs.text: This page covers how to run tests, check coverage, and documents known gotchas encountered during development.

docs.title: Unit Tests
docs.text:
make test

Runs go test ./... across all packages. No external dependencies or built binaries required.

docs.title: Integration Tests
docs.text:
make test-integration

Runs go test -tags integration ./.... The plugin integration tests build the plugins they need (for example plugins/example) with go build, so no pre-built binaries are required. Tests that need external services skip themselves when the service is not available: the S3 backend and pruner tests expect MinIO at localhost:9000, and the Sentinel cloud tests need cloud credentials and bucket variables such as HITSTOR_GCS_BUCKET or HITSTOR_S3_BUCKET.

.github/workflows/release.yml runs go test ./... (unit tests only) before building a release.

docs.title: Linting
docs.text:
make lint

Runs go vet ./... to catch common issues.

docs.title: Code Coverage
docs.text:
Generate a coverage report and view it in the browser:

go test -coverprofile=coverage.out ./...
go tool cover -html=coverage.out

Target: 80%+ per package.

docs.title: Known Gotchas
docs.text:
Issues encountered during development that are worth remembering:

Issue Solution go-plugin v1.7.0 GRPCClient signature First parameter must be context.Context bufconn gRPC tests fail silently on large messages Raise the limits on both sides: grpc.MaxRecvMsgSize/grpc.MaxSendMsgSize on the test server and grpc.MaxCallRecvMsgSize/grpc.MaxCallSendMsgSize in the client's default call options (the tests use math.MaxInt32) Plugin proto cross-file imports fail Use the -I api/proto include path (already in the proto-plugin Makefile target) Streaming differs between plugin types The scanner's Scan and the workload Backup stream from the plugin, and workload Restore streams to it; storage, notifier, and hook plugins use unary RPCs only Test breakage after scanner type refactor Use type ScanResult = scanner.ScanResult (type alias) instead of a new type

docs.title: Translations
docs.text: HitStor's web dashboard and this documentation are available in English and Spanish. Both are built so that more languages can be added without code changes. Account emails (invitations, password resets) and PDF reports use the same message catalogs: an account email is written in the language of the dashboard page that triggers it, and each scheduled report (and its email) has its own language setting. The CLI, installers and log messages stay in English.

docs.title: Choosing the language
docs.text:
The dashboard picks the language for each browser in this order:

  1. The language chosen with the selector in the header (or on the login page), stored in the hitstor_lang cookie.
  2. The server default, serve_dashboard_language in the server's config.yaml (for example es).
  3. The browser's preferred languages (Accept-Language).
  4. English.
hitstor config set serve_dashboard_language es

Restart the server after changing the default.

docs.title: How messages are stored
docs.text:
Messages are keyed by their English text. English needs no catalog, and any message without a translation is shown in English.

Each language is a directory under internal/i18n/locales/:

internal/i18n/locales/
├── en/
│   └── _meta.json
└── es/
    ├── _meta.json
    ├── common.json
    ├── login.json
    └── ...            one fragment per dashboard area

_meta.json names the language:

{"code": "es", "name": "Español", "complete": true}

Fragments map English text to the translation. Placeholders in braces must be kept:

{
  "Backups": "Respaldos",
  "{n} days ago": "hace {n} días"
}

In templates, text is marked with {{t "Backups"}} or {{tf "{n} days ago" "n" .Days}}. In JavaScript, with t('Backups') or t('{n} days ago', {n: days}).

docs.title: Adding a language
docs.text:
1. Create internal/i18n/locales/<code>/_meta.json with "complete": false (the code is the language tag browsers send, e.g. fr or pt-BR).
  2. Copy the Spanish fragments as a starting point and translate the values, keeping the English keys and the {placeholders}.

  3. Run the catalog tests:

    go test ./internal/i18n/ ./internal/dashboard/ -run 'TestCatalog|TestNegotiate'

    TestCatalogsComplete lists untranslated messages for languages marked "complete": true and, for every language, translations that are no longer used. TestCatalogPlaceholders checks the placeholders.

  4. When every message is translated, set "complete": true so the tests keep the language complete as the dashboard changes.

  5. Rebuild the server. The new language appears in the selector automatically.

docs.title: When you change dashboard text
docs.text: Every new or changed English message must be added to each complete language; TestCatalogsComplete fails until it is. Messages shown from runtime values (for example job statuses translated with {{t .Status}}) are listed one per line in internal/dashboard/i18n-dynamic/*.txt so the test knows they are used.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
The site uses mkdocs-static-i18n with one file per language next to each page: quickstart.md (English) and quickstart.es.md (Spanish). A page without a translation falls back to English.

  • Keep the English anchors on translated headings so links work in every language: ## Inicio rápido { #quick-start }.
  • Keep link targets pointing to the English file names (quickstart.md#dashboard-password); the plugin maps them to the right language.
  • Menu titles for each language are set under nav_translations in mkdocs.yml.
  • Terminology for Spanish is in the Spanish glossary.

To add a documentation language, add it under the i18n plugin's languages in mkdocs.yml and create <page>.<code>.md files.

Build the site locally:

pip install -r requirements-docs.txt
make docs-build

docs.title: Repository files
docs.text: README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md and benchmarks/README.md have Spanish versions (*.es.md) linked from the first line of each file.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
HitStor provides two binaries:

  • hitstor -- the backup server, CLI tool, and web dashboard.
  • hitstor-agent -- a lightweight remote agent that sends encrypted, deduplicated backups to a HitStor server over gRPC.

Choose the installation method that best fits your environment.

New to HitStor? Start with the Quick Start guide — Docker server + agent binaries in ~15 minutes.

docs.title: Installation Methods
docs.text: Method Platforms Best For Quick Start Docker + Linux/Windows agents Fastest path: Docker server, VM installer, or agent-only Linux Quick Install (.run) Ubuntu, Debian, RHEL, Fedora, AlmaLinux Interactive wizard — configures, initializes, and starts everything. Built-in upgrade with rollback and uninstaller. Linux Packages (deb/rpm) Debian, Ubuntu, RHEL, Fedora, AlmaLinux Production servers with package manager Build from Source Linux or Windows, Go 1.26+ Development, custom builds, unsupported architectures Windows Server Windows 10+, Windows Server 2016+ Running the HitStor server on Windows Windows Agent Windows 10+, Windows Server 2016+ Backing up Windows machines to a remote HitStor server Docker Any Docker host Containerized deployment, CI/CD pipelines

docs.title: After Installation
docs.text:
Once HitStor is installed, continue with:

  1. Getting Started -- end-to-end tutorial covering init, backup, restore, verify, and prune.
  2. Configuration -- config file schema, environment variables, and flag precedence.
  3. Command Reference -- detailed documentation for every command.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text: See Upgrading for instructions on upgrading an existing HitStor installation.

docs.title: Docker Deployment
docs.text: HitStor provides a multi-stage Dockerfile that produces a minimal Alpine-based container image. The image runs the HitStor server with gRPC and web dashboard support.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Docker 20.10+ or a compatible container runtime
  • Docker Compose v2 (for the compose-based deployment)

docs.title: Build the Image
docs.text:
From the repository root:

docker build -t hitstor:latest .

To build with a specific version tag:

docker build -t hitstor:0.2.0 \
  --build-arg VERSION=0.2.0 \
  --build-arg COMMIT=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) \
  --build-arg DATE=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d) .

Or use the Makefile target:

make docker-build VERSION=0.2.0

docs.title: Image Details
docs.text:
The Docker image uses a two-stage build:

  1. Builder stage -- golang:1.26-alpine compiles the static binary with CGO_ENABLED=0.
  2. Runtime stage -- alpine:3.22 with only ca-certificates, tzdata, and wget (for the health check) installed. All HitStor binaries from cmd/ are copied to /usr/bin.

The image runs as a non-root hitstor user.

Property Value Base image alpine:3.22 User hitstor Exposed ports 8420 (gRPC), 8421 (dashboard) Volumes /var/lib/hitstor (data), /etc/hitstor (config) Entrypoint /entrypoint.sh Default command serve

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
For the full end-to-end guide (Docker server + agent installation), see Quick Start.

Run the server directly with Docker:

docker run -d \
  --name hitstor \
  -p 8420:8420 \
  -p 8421:8421 \
  -v hitstor-data:/var/lib/hitstor \
  -e HITSTOR_PASSWORD=my-secret-password \
  -e HITSTOR_REPO=/var/lib/hitstor/repo \
  hitstor:latest

On first start the entrypoint runs hitstor init for HITSTOR_REPO if no repository exists there, then hitstor serve. Open https://<host>:8421 (self-signed certificate) and create the first administrator as described in Dashboard Password and First Administrator. Without HITSTOR_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD the container has no config file to save a generated password to, so read it from docker logs hitstor.

docs.title: Quickstart (local repository)
docs.text:
For evaluation and homelab use:

cp .env.example .env
# edit HITSTOR_PASSWORD
docker compose -f docker-compose.quickstart.yml up -d

See Quick Start for agent setup and the optional MinIO (--profile s3) stack.

docs.title: Production
docs.text: The production deployment uses docker-compose.prod.yml:

docs.title: 1. Create the Configuration Directory
docs.text:
mkdir -p config

Place your config.yaml in this directory. You can copy and edit the example:

cp packaging/config/server-config.yaml.example config/config.yaml
editor config/config.yaml

docs.title: 2. Set Environment Variables
docs.text:
Create a .env file in the repository root:

HITSTOR_VERSION=latest
HITSTOR_PASSWORD=my-secret-password

Or export the variables in your shell before running docker compose.

docs.title: 3. Start the Services
docs.text: docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d

docs.title: 4. Verify
docs.text:
Check that the container is running and healthy:

docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml ps

The health check uses wget to poll the dashboard on port 8421 every 30 seconds.

View the logs:

docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml logs -f

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Port Protocol Description 8420 TCP gRPC server -- agent connections and CLI operations 8421 TCP Web dashboard

docs.title: Volumes
docs.text: Mount Point Description /var/lib/hitstor Repository data. This is where encrypted backup packs, indexes, and snapshots are stored. Use a named volume or bind mount to persistent storage. /etc/hitstor Configuration files. Mounted read-only from the host config/ directory.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Description HITSTOR_PASSWORD Repository password used for encryption and decryption. HITSTOR_REPO Path to the repository inside the container. The compose files set /var/lib/hitstor/repo; the image has no default. HITSTOR_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD Dashboard setup password, used to create the first administrator. The entrypoint writes it to /etc/hitstor/config.yaml when that file does not exist yet. HITSTOR_AUTO_INIT true (default) runs hitstor init for HITSTOR_REPO on start when no repository exists; false skips it. HITSTOR_VERSION Image version tag used by the compose files.

docs.title: Health Check
docs.text:
The production compose file includes a built-in health check:

healthcheck:
  test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -q -O /dev/null --no-check-certificate https://localhost:8421/login || wget -q -O /dev/null http://localhost:8421/login"]
  interval: 30s
  timeout: 5s
  retries: 3

Use docker inspect or docker compose ps to check the health status. The check requests the sign-in page over HTTPS (with the self-signed certificate) and falls back to plain HTTP, which the dashboard serves only while no repository exists.

docs.title: Saving the Image
docs.text:
To export the image as a tarball for offline deployment:

make docker-save VERSION=0.2.0

This writes dist/hitstor-0.2.0-docker.tar.gz. Load it on the target host with:

docker load < hitstor-0.2.0-docker.tar.gz

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Getting Started -- initialize a repository and create your first backup.
  • Configuration -- full config file reference.
  • Upgrading -- how to upgrade a Docker deployment.

docs.title: Linux Quick Install
docs.text:
The fastest way to install HitStor on a Linux server. Download a single .run file, execute it, and the interactive wizard configures everything — no package manager, no build tools, no dependencies.

Requirements

  • Linux (amd64 or arm64)
  • systemd
  • Root privileges (sudo)
  • Tested on Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12+, RHEL 9+, Fedora 39+, AlmaLinux 9+

docs.title: Install the Server
docs.text:
Download the installer from the GitHub Releases page and run it:

wget https://github.com/hooperits/hitstor/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/hitstor-server-X.Y.Z-linux-amd64.run
chmod +x hitstor-server-X.Y.Z-linux-amd64.run
sudo ./hitstor-server-X.Y.Z-linux-amd64.run

The interactive wizard will prompt for:

  1. Data directory — where HitStor stores data (default: /var/lib/hitstor)
  2. Dashboard password — the setup password for the web UI, used until the first administrator account exists (optional; if empty, the server generates one on first start — see Dashboard Password and First Administrator)
  3. gRPC port — for agent connections (default: 8420)
  4. Dashboard port — for the web UI (default: 8421)
  5. Server advertise address — the address sent to agents so they can reach the server (default: the detected outbound IP and the gRPC port)

After confirming, the installer creates the system user, starts the service, and verifies everything is running. Repositories are created from the dashboard after installation; after creating the first one, restart the service (sudo systemctl restart hitstor-server) and create the first administrator.

docs.title: Non-Interactive Install
docs.text:
For automation, use --no-wizard with environment variables:

sudo HITSTOR_DATA_DIR=/var/lib/hitstor \
     HITSTOR_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD=dashpass \
     HITSTOR_GRPC_PORT=8420 \
     HITSTOR_DASHBOARD_PORT=8421 \
     HITSTOR_ADVERTISE_ADDR=192.0.2.10:8420 \
     ./hitstor-server-X.Y.Z-linux-amd64.run --no-wizard

HITSTOR_ADVERTISE_ADDR is optional; when unset, the installer detects the outbound IP.

docs.title: Installed Files
docs.text: Path Description /usr/bin/hitstor Server binary /usr/lib/systemd/system/hitstor-server.service systemd service unit /etc/hitstor/config.yaml Server configuration /etc/hitstor/server.env Environment variables /var/lib/hitstor/ Data directory (default path) /var/log/hitstor/ Log directory

docs.title: Install the Agent
docs.text:
Download the agent installer and run it:

wget https://github.com/hooperits/hitstor/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/hitstor-agent-X.Y.Z-linux-amd64.run
chmod +x hitstor-agent-X.Y.Z-linux-amd64.run
sudo ./hitstor-agent-X.Y.Z-linux-amd64.run

The agent is managed from the dashboard. The wizard asks only for the listen port (default: 8422), the port the server connects to for registration, browsing, and backup triggers. It then installs and starts the hitstor-agent service, which generates the agent token on first start.

After installation the installer displays the agent token and the next steps: in the dashboard, go to Agents → Add Agent and enter this machine's IP address, the listen port, and the token. Backup paths and schedules are configured from the dashboard.

docs.title: Non-Interactive Install
docs.text:
sudo HITSTOR_AGENT_LISTEN_PORT=8422 \
     ./hitstor-agent-X.Y.Z-linux-amd64.run --no-wizard

docs.title: Installed Files
docs.text: Path Description /usr/bin/hitstor-agent Agent binary /usr/lib/systemd/system/hitstor-agent.service systemd service unit /etc/hitstor/agent-config.yaml Agent configuration /etc/hitstor/agent.env Environment variables (listen port, server address) /etc/hitstor/agent-token Agent token for dashboard registration (mode 0600)

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
Running the installer on an existing installation automatically detects the upgrade:

sudo ./hitstor-server-X.Y.Z-linux-amd64.run

The upgrade process:

  1. Displays the current and new version for confirmation
  2. Backs up the current binary to /usr/bin/hitstor.rollback
  3. Stops the service (if running)
  4. Installs the new binary and systemd units
  5. Updates example config files (your working configs are never touched)
  6. Restarts the service and verifies it is healthy
  7. On verification failure: automatically rolls back to the previous version

Use --no-wizard to skip the confirmation prompt (for automation).

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text: The v2 installer includes a built-in uninstaller:

docs.title: Server
docs.text:
sudo ./hitstor-server-X.Y.Z-linux-amd64.run --uninstall

This removes the binary, systemd service, configuration, logs, and system user. You will be asked separately whether to remove the data directory (/var/lib/hitstor) — default is no to protect your backups.

docs.title: Agent
docs.text:
sudo ./hitstor-agent-X.Y.Z-linux-amd64.run --uninstall

This removes the binary, systemd service/timer, and configuration.

docs.title: Version Check
docs.text: HitStor can check for newer versions via the GitHub Releases API.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text: hitstor version --check

docs.title: Automatic (Server)
docs.text: When update_check: true is set in /etc/hitstor/config.yaml (it is off unless set; it can also be turned on under Settings → General), the server checks for updates every 24 hours. If a newer version is available, a banner appears at the top of the web dashboard.

docs.title: ARM64 Support
docs.text:
ARM64 (aarch64) installers are also available. Download the arm64 variant:

sudo ./hitstor-server-X.Y.Z-linux-arm64.run
sudo ./hitstor-agent-X.Y.Z-linux-arm64.run

docs.title: Installer Flags
docs.text: Flag Description --no-wizard Non-interactive mode (reads from environment variables) --uninstall Remove HitStor and all associated files --yes Skip confirmation prompts (with --uninstall) --version Print installer version and exit --help Show help

docs.title: Permission Denied
docs.text:
The installer must be run as root:

sudo ./hitstor-server-X.Y.Z-linux-amd64.run

docs.title: systemd Not Found
docs.text: The .run installer requires systemd. If your system does not have systemd, use the Build from Source method and manage the process manually.

docs.title: Status 226/NAMESPACE
docs.text:
On some virtualized environments (Hyper-V VMs, containers, WSL), systemd security hardening may cause the service to fail with exit code 226. To fix this, edit the service unit and comment out the hardening directives:

sudo systemctl edit hitstor-server

Add the following overrides:

[Service]
ProtectSystem=
ProtectHome=
ProtectKernelTunables=
ProtectKernelModules=
ProtectControlGroups=
PrivateTmp=
NoNewPrivileges=

Then restart:

sudo systemctl restart hitstor-server

See Troubleshooting for more details.

docs.title: Linux Packages (deb/rpm)
docs.text:
Pre-built packages for Debian/Ubuntu (.deb) and RHEL/Fedora/AlmaLinux (.rpm) in amd64 architecture.

Prefer the .run installer for easier setup

The Linux Quick Install (.run) provides an interactive wizard that configures the dashboard password, ports, advertise address, and service startup for you. Packages require manual configuration (see below).

docs.title: Download
docs.text:
Download the latest packages from the GitHub Releases page. Each release includes four Linux packages:

Package Description hitstor_x.y.z_amd64.deb Server -- Debian/Ubuntu hitstor-x.y.z-1.x86_64.rpm Server -- RHEL/Fedora/AlmaLinux hitstor-agent_x.y.z_amd64.deb Agent -- Debian/Ubuntu hitstor-agent-x.y.z-1.x86_64.rpm Agent -- RHEL/Fedora/AlmaLinux

docs.title: Install the Server
docs.text:
Debian / UbuntuRHEL / Fedora 
sudo dpkg -i hitstor_x.y.z_amd64.deb

sudo rpm -i hitstor-x.y.z-1.x86_64.rpm

The package installs:

Path Description /usr/bin/hitstor Server binary /usr/lib/systemd/system/hitstor-server.service systemd service unit /etc/hitstor/server.env.example Environment file template /etc/hitstor/config.yaml.example Configuration file template

docs.title: Install the Agent
docs.text:
Debian / UbuntuRHEL / Fedora 
sudo dpkg -i hitstor-agent_x.y.z_amd64.deb

sudo rpm -i hitstor-agent-x.y.z-1.x86_64.rpm

The agent package installs:

Path Description /usr/bin/hitstor-agent Agent binary /usr/lib/systemd/system/hitstor-agent.service systemd service unit /etc/hitstor/agent.env.example Environment file template /etc/hitstor/agent-config.yaml.example Configuration file template /usr/lib/hitstor/plugins/hitstor-scanner-builtin Built-in filesystem scanner plugin /var/lib/hitstor/plugins/ Store for workload plugins (mode 0700)

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: The packages' post-install scripts copy the examples to the working files (server.env, config.yaml, agent.env, agent-config.yaml) when those do not exist yet, and never overwrite them on upgrade. The server package also creates the hitstor system user.

docs.title: Server
docs.text:
Edit /etc/hitstor/config.yaml to configure the server (ports, advertise address, TLS certificates, dashboard settings, etc.):

sudo editor /etc/hitstor/config.yaml

Repositories are normally created from the dashboard Storage page after the service starts. /etc/hitstor/server.env only needs HITSTOR_REPO and HITSTOR_PASSWORD for the legacy single-repository mode. The first sign-in works as described in Dashboard Password and First Administrator.

docs.title: Agent
docs.text:
For a dashboard-managed agent (recommended), keep the copied files as they are: start the service (below), read the token with sudo hitstor-agent show-id, and add the agent from the dashboard (Agents → Add Agent) with its IP address, listen port (default 8422), and token.

Edit /etc/hitstor/agent.env only for a manually registered agent, to set HITSTOR_AGENT_SERVER and HITSTOR_AGENT_API_KEY (the key printed by hitstor serve agent add <name>):

sudo editor /etc/hitstor/agent.env

docs.title: Server
docs.text:
Enable and start the HitStor server:

sudo systemctl enable --now hitstor-server

Check the service status:

sudo systemctl status hitstor-server

View logs:

journalctl -u hitstor-server -f

docs.title: Agent
docs.text:
Enable and start the HitStor agent:

sudo systemctl enable --now hitstor-agent

docs.title: Verify the Installation
docs.text:
hitstor version

This prints the version, commit hash, and build date. If the command is not found, ensure /usr/bin is in your PATH.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
Debian / UbuntuRHEL / Fedora 
sudo systemctl disable --now hitstor-server
sudo dpkg -r hitstor

sudo systemctl disable --now hitstor-server
sudo rpm -e hitstor

Configuration files in /etc/hitstor/ are preserved during removal. Delete them manually if no longer needed.

docs.title: Build from Source
docs.text: Building from source is recommended for development, testing, or when pre-built packages are not available for your platform. HitStor compiles with CGO_ENABLED=0, producing fully static binaries with no runtime dependencies.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Go 1.26+ -- HitStor uses log/slog and other features from recent Go releases.
  • git -- to clone the repository.
  • make -- to use the provided build targets (optional but recommended).

docs.title: Clone the Repository
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/hooperits/hitstor.git
cd hitstor

docs.title: Server
docs.text:
make build

The binary is written to bin/hitstor.

docs.title: Agent
docs.text:
make agent

The binary is written to bin/hitstor-agent.

docs.title: Build Without Make
docs.text:
If you prefer to build manually:

# Server
CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o bin/hitstor ./cmd/hitstor/

# Agent
CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o bin/hitstor-agent ./cmd/hitstor-agent/

docs.title: Cross-Compilation
docs.text:
Because HitStor compiles with CGO_ENABLED=0, cross-compilation is straightforward. The Makefile includes targets for common platforms:

# Linux ARM64 (Raspberry Pi, AWS Graviton)
make build-arm64
make agent-arm64

# Windows amd64 (server and agent)
make build-windows
make agent-windows

# Windows ARM64 (agent)
make agent-windows-arm64

To cross-compile manually, set GOOS and GOARCH:

GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o bin/hitstor.exe ./cmd/hitstor/

Linux and Windows are the supported targets; other operating systems (for example macOS or FreeBSD) do not build.

The resulting binary is a single static file with no external dependencies.

docs.title: Workload Plugin Packages
docs.text:
Workload plugins such as mssql are built and packaged separately:

make plugin-packages PLUGIN_UNSIGNED=1   # unsigned, for local testing
make plugin-packages PLUGIN_KEY_FILE=mykey.key

This writes one .hpk package per target in WORKLOAD_PLUGIN_TARGETS to dist/, named hitstor-plugin-<id>-<version>-<os>-<arch>.hpk. Agents accept unsigned packages only with plugin_allow_unsigned: true. See Plugin Development.

docs.title: Install to PATH
docs.text:
Copy the binary to a directory in your $PATH:

sudo cp bin/hitstor /usr/local/bin/
sudo cp bin/hitstor-agent /usr/local/bin/

docs.title: Verify the Build
docs.text:
hitstor version

This prints the version, commit hash, and build date. During development builds, the version is reported as dev.

You can also verify with:

hitstor --help

docs.title: Running Tests
docs.text:
To run the test suite after building:

make test

For integration tests:

make test-integration

docs.title: Build All Targets
docs.text:
To build the server and agent for Linux (amd64, arm64) and Windows in a single command:

make build-all

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Getting Started -- initialize a repository and create your first backup.
  • Configuration -- set up a config file to avoid repeating flags.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Get HitStor running in about 15 minutes. This guide covers the four recommended paths for early adopters:

  1. Docker — fastest way to run the server (developers and homelab)
  2. Linux VM installer — production-style server on a single machine
  3. Windows Server installer — server as a Windows Service
  4. Agent only — connect laptops and servers to an existing HitStor server

Agents are always native binaries installed on each machine you want to back up. The server can run in Docker or on a VM.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Docker 20.10+ and Docker Compose v2
  • 2 GB RAM and a few GB of free disk for the repository volume

docs.title: 1. Configure environment
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/hooperits/hitstor.git
cd hitstor
cp .env.example .env

Edit .env and set a strong HITSTOR_PASSWORD (repository encryption) and HITSTOR_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD (the setup password you use once to create the first dashboard administrator). If you leave HITSTOR_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD empty, the server generates a new random one on every container start — see Dashboard Password and First Administrator.

docs.title: 2. Start the server
docs.text:
docker compose -f docker-compose.quickstart.yml up -d

On first start, the container automatically runs hitstor init and then hitstor serve.

docs.title: 3. Open the dashboard
docs.text:
Navigate to https://localhost:8421 (the certificate is self-signed, so the browser warns the first time). The dashboard opens at Create the first administrator: enter HITSTOR_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD (or the generated password), choose your user name and password, and set up an authenticator app. See Dashboard Password and First Administrator.

Port Service 8421 Web dashboard 8420 gRPC (agents connect here)

docs.title: 4. Install an agent
docs.text: On each machine to back up, install the agent binary. See Path D below.

docs.title: Optional: S3 storage with MinIO
docs.text:
To store backups in S3-compatible storage instead of a local Docker volume:

docker compose -f docker-compose.quickstart.yml --profile s3 up -d

This starts HitStor with s3:http://minio:9000/hitstor-backups and a bundled MinIO instance. The MinIO console is at http://localhost:9001 (minioadmin / minioadmin).

Development only

The bundled MinIO credentials are for local testing. Do not expose this stack to the internet without changing credentials and enabling TLS.

docs.title: Pull a pre-built image
docs.text:
Release images are published to GHCR (ghcr.io/hooperits/hitstor, tagged with the release version and latest):

export HITSTOR_IMAGE=ghcr.io/hooperits/hitstor
export HITSTOR_VERSION=latest
docker compose -f docker-compose.quickstart.yml up -d

Build locally instead:

docker compose -f docker-compose.quickstart.yml build
docker compose -f docker-compose.quickstart.yml up -d

docs.title: Stop and remove
docs.text:
docker compose -f docker-compose.quickstart.yml down
# Add -v to delete repository data volumes

docs.title: Path B: Linux VM Installer
docs.text: Use this when you prefer a native server install without Docker — typical for a dedicated backup VM.

docs.title: 1. Download the server installer
docs.text:
From GitHub Releases:

wget https://github.com/hooperits/hitstor/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/hitstor-server-X.Y.Z-linux-amd64.run
chmod +x hitstor-server-*.run
sudo ./hitstor-server-*.run

The interactive wizard asks for the data directory, an optional dashboard setup password, the ports, and the address agents use to reach the server; it then configures systemd and starts the server. It does not create a repository: you do that from the dashboard.

docs.title: 2. Open the dashboard
docs.text:
Open http://<server-ip>:8421 and sign in with the dashboard password you entered in the wizard (if you left it empty, see Dashboard Password and First Administrator). Until a repository exists the server runs in setup mode over plain HTTP. Create a repository from the Storage page and restart the service (sudo systemctl restart hitstor-server): the dashboard then switches to HTTPS (https://<server-ip>:8421, self-signed by default) and opens at Create the first administrator.

See Linux Quick Install for wizard details and Server Setup for production hardening.

docs.title: 3. Install agents
docs.text: Continue with Path D.

docs.title: Path C: Windows Server Installer
docs.text: Use this to run the server on Windows Server 2016+ (or Windows 10 1809+) as a Windows Service.

docs.title: 1. Run the installer
docs.text:
Download hitstor-X.Y.Z-windows-amd64-setup.exe from GitHub Releases and run it as Administrator, or install unattended from an elevated PowerShell:

.\hitstor-X.Y.Z-windows-amd64-setup.exe /S

The installer copies hitstor.exe to C:\Program Files\HitStor, creates C:\ProgramData\HitStor\config.yaml, adds firewall rules for ports 8420 and 8421, and registers and starts the HitStor service. Running a newer installer the same way upgrades in place.

docs.title: 2. Get the dashboard password
docs.text: The server generates a random dashboard setup password on first start. Read it on the server as described in Dashboard Password and First Administrator.

docs.title: 3. Open the dashboard
docs.text:
Open http://<server-ip>:8421, sign in with that password, and create a repository from the Storage page. Until a repository exists the server runs in setup mode and serves the dashboard over plain HTTP; HTTPS (self-signed by default) is enabled after a repository is configured and the service restarts (Restart-Service HitStor). After the restart, open https://<server-ip>:8421 and create the first administrator (see Dashboard Password and First Administrator).

See Windows Server for service management and firewall details.

docs.title: 4. Install agents
docs.text: Continue with Path D.

docs.title: Path D: Agent Only
docs.text: Install hitstor-agent on every machine whose data you want in the repository.

docs.title: Linux
docs.text:
wget https://github.com/hooperits/hitstor/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/hitstor-agent-X.Y.Z-linux-amd64.run
chmod +x hitstor-agent-*.run
sudo ./hitstor-agent-*.run

The wizard asks only for the agent's listen port (default 8422), installs the service, and prints the agent token. In the HitStor dashboard:

  1. Go to Agents → Add Agent
  2. Enter the agent's IP address, its listen port, and the token
  3. Create a backup job under Backups

For scripted installs:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hooperits/hitstor/master/scripts/install-agent.sh | sudo bash

See Agent Deployment for daemon mode and Windows, and SQL Server for database backups through the mssql workload plugin.

docs.title: Windows
docs.text: Download hitstor-agent-X.Y.Z-windows-amd64-setup.exe from Releases and run the installer. See Windows Agent.

docs.title: Verify connectivity
docs.text: From the agent host, the server gRPC port must be reachable (default 8420). Agents poll the server for backup schedules; you can also trigger Backup Now from the dashboard.

docs.title: Dashboard Password and First Administrator
docs.text:
The dashboard uses personal accounts, each with its own password, roles, and mandatory two-step verification (see Users and Access). A new server has no accounts yet, so it starts with a single dashboard password (the serve_dashboard_password setting) that is only used to get to the first administrator:

  1. No repository yet (setup mode): sign in with the dashboard password and create a repository under Storage, then restart the server. Accounts are stored next to the first repository, so they can only exist once it does.
  2. Repository, no accounts: every page leads to Create the first administrator (/setup). Enter the current dashboard password, choose the administrator's user name and password (at least 12 characters), then scan the QR code with an authenticator app and save the recovery codes.
  3. Accounts exist: everyone signs in with their own user name, password, and a code. The dashboard password no longer signs in. Add more users under Users and access.

HitStor has no default dashboard password. The password comes from:

Install path Source Docker HITSTOR_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD in .env Linux VM installer The password entered in the wizard Windows installer Generated on first start

When the config file has no dashboard password, hitstor serve generates a random one at startup, saves its hash to the config file (when the server has one; otherwise a new password is generated at every start), and writes the plaintext once to the server log, in an entry that contains no dashboard password configured; generated one. You do not need dashboard access to read it — read the log on the server.

docs.title: Read the generated password
docs.text:
Windows (PowerShell as Administrator; the log is readable only by Administrators and SYSTEM):

Select-String -Path C:\ProgramData\HitStor\logs\server.log -Pattern 'generated one' |
  Select-Object -Last 1 |
  ForEach-Object { ($_.Line | ConvertFrom-Json).fields.password }

Linux:

sudo grep 'generated one' /var/log/hitstor/server.log | tail -1
# or
sudo journalctl -u hitstor-server | grep 'generated one' | tail -1

Docker:

docker compose -f docker-compose.quickstart.yml logs hitstor | grep 'generated one' | tail -1

Copy and paste the value rather than typing it — generated passwords mix characters that look alike (l/I, O/0).

Use it to sign in while the server has no repository, and to create the first administrator. The log keeps the original entry, so if you change the password under Settings before that, the logged value no longer works.

docs.title: Create the first administrator from the console
docs.text:
Instead of the /setup page, you can create the first administrator on the server with hitstor serve user add. Run it with the same configuration as the service: it uses the repository where the server keeps its users (the first one by name) and prints a temporary password, and at the first sign-in the user chooses their own password and sets up the authenticator:

# Linux
sudo -u hitstor hitstor --config /etc/hitstor/config.yaml serve user add admin --grant admin

# Docker quick start (the container already has HITSTOR_REPO and HITSTOR_PASSWORD)
docker compose -f docker-compose.quickstart.yml exec hitstor hitstor serve user add admin --grant admin

The same command family resets a password (serve user passwd) or two-step verification (serve user reset-2fa) when no administrator can sign in.

docs.title: Reset a lost password
docs.text:
This applies to the dashboard password, before the first administrator exists. Once there are accounts, reset a user's password with hitstor serve user passwd <name> (see Users and Access).

Remove the stored password from the config file and restart the server; a new password is generated and logged as above.

Windows:

Stop-Service HitStor
$cfg = 'C:\ProgramData\HitStor\config.yaml'
(Get-Content $cfg) -notmatch '^serve_dashboard_password:' | Set-Content $cfg -Encoding ascii
Start-Service HitStor

Linux:

sudo sed -i '/^serve_dashboard_password:/d' /etc/hitstor/config.yaml
sudo systemctl restart hitstor-server

Docker: set a new HITSTOR_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD in .env and recreate the container (docker compose -f docker-compose.quickstart.yml up -d --force-recreate).

docs.title: First Backup Checklist
docs.text:
After server and at least one agent are connected:

  1. Storage — confirm a repository exists (Docker quickstart creates one automatically; with the VM and Windows installers you create it from the dashboard)
  2. Agents — agent shows as connected in the dashboard
  3. Backups — create a job and assign it to the agent: a file backup, or a workload job such as SQL Server with a backup plan of full, differential, and log schedules
  4. Run — click Backup Now or wait for the schedule
  5. Restore — test a restore from the dashboard or CLI

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Getting Started — backup, restore, retention
  • Docker Deployment — production compose, image details, offline export
  • Agent Deployment — production agent setup
  • Configuration — config file reference

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text: This page covers how to upgrade an existing HitStor installation. Repositories are forward-compatible: newer versions of HitStor can read and write repositories created by older versions without any migration steps.

docs.title: Before You Upgrade
docs.text:
1. Check your current version and available updates:

    hitstor version
hitstor version --check

    Tip

    With update_check: true in the server configuration (or Settings → General), the server checks for updates every 24 hours and displays a banner in the web dashboard when a newer version is available. The check is off unless enabled.

  2. Back up your configuration files. While upgrades preserve configuration, it is good practice to save a copy before proceeding:

    # Linux
sudo cp -r /etc/hitstor /etc/hitstor.bak

# Windows (PowerShell)
Copy-Item -Recurse "$env:ProgramData\HitStor" "$env:ProgramData\HitStor.bak"

  3. Review the release notes on the GitHub Releases page for any breaking changes or required manual steps.

docs.title: Linux Quick Install (.run)
docs.text:
Run the new .run installer on an existing installation. The installer automatically detects the upgrade, displays the version comparison, and handles the entire process:

sudo ./hitstor-server-X.Y.Z-linux-amd64.run

The upgrade process:

  1. Displays current and new version for confirmation
  2. Backs up the current binary
  3. Stops the service, installs the new binary and systemd units
  4. Never overwrites your working configuration files (only updates example files)
  5. Restarts the service and verifies it is healthy
  6. On verification failure: automatically rolls back to the previous version

Use --no-wizard to skip the confirmation prompt for automated upgrades.

The same process works for the agent:

sudo ./hitstor-agent-X.Y.Z-linux-amd64.run

docs.title: Linux Packages
docs.text:
Download the new package from GitHub Releases and install it over the existing one.

Debian / UbuntuRHEL / Fedora 
sudo dpkg -i hitstor_x.y.z_amd64.deb

sudo rpm -U hitstor-x.y.z-1.x86_64.rpm

The same applies to the agent package:

Debian / UbuntuRHEL / Fedora 
sudo dpkg -i hitstor-agent_x.y.z_amd64.deb

sudo rpm -U hitstor-agent-x.y.z-1.x86_64.rpm

Restart the services after upgrading:

sudo systemctl restart hitstor-server
sudo systemctl restart hitstor-agent

Verify the new version:

hitstor version

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
Rebuild the image and restart the container:

# Pull latest source (if building from source)
git pull

# Rebuild the image
docker build -t hitstor:latest .

# Restart with the new image
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml down
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d

Or, if using a specific version tag:

docker build -t hitstor:0.2.0 \
  --build-arg VERSION=0.2.0 \
  --build-arg COMMIT=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) \
  --build-arg DATE=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d) .

Update the HITSTOR_VERSION variable in your .env file, then:

docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml down
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d

Verify:

docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml exec hitstor hitstor version

Repository data in the /var/lib/hitstor volume is preserved across container restarts.

docs.title: Windows
docs.text:
Run the new installer over the existing installation. The NSIS installer overwrites the previous binary and updates the registry entries while preserving your configuration files in %ProgramData%\HitStor\.

  1. Download the new installer from GitHub Releases.

  2. Run the installer:

    hitstor-x.y.z-windows-amd64-setup.exe

  3. Follow the installation wizard. Use the same installation directory as the previous version.

  4. Open a new PowerShell window and verify:

    hitstor version

For the agent, download and run the agent installer:

hitstor-agent-x.y.z-windows-amd64-setup.exe

If the agent is running as a Windows Service, it is automatically stopped during the upgrade and restarted afterward.

docs.title: Build from Source
docs.text:
Pull the latest changes and rebuild:

cd /path/to/hitstor
git pull
make build
make agent

Replace the installed binaries:

sudo cp bin/hitstor /usr/local/bin/
sudo cp bin/hitstor-agent /usr/local/bin/

Verify:

hitstor version

If running as a systemd service, restart it:

sudo systemctl restart hitstor-server

docs.title: After Upgrading from 0.1.x
docs.text:
Version 0.2.0 replaces the single shared dashboard password with personal accounts, roles, and mandatory two-step verification. After the upgrade, the dashboard opens at Create the first administrator:

  1. Enter the current dashboard password (the one you set in serve_dashboard_password, or the one the server printed in its log).
  2. Choose the administrator's user name and password (at least 12 characters).
  3. Scan the QR code with an authenticator app, enter a code, and save the recovery codes.

From then on the shared password no longer signs in. Create accounts for the other people who use the dashboard under Users and access, or with hitstor serve user add on the server. Accounts are stored in the first repository, next to the agent registry. See Users and Access.

docs.title: Repository Compatibility
docs.text:
HitStor repositories are forward-compatible. A repository created with an older version can be read and written by any newer version without migration. There is no separate migration command or repository upgrade step.

If a future release ever requires a repository format change, it will be documented in the release notes with explicit migration instructions.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
Linux Quick Install (.run): The .run installer automatically rolls back if post-upgrade verification fails. The previous binary is restored and the service is restarted with the old version — no manual intervention needed.

Other methods: If you need to revert to a previous version, install the older package or binary using the same installation method and restart the service.

Repositories are forward-compatible, so rolling back to an older version is safe as long as no forward-incompatible repository format changes were introduced (which would be documented in the release notes).

docs.title: Windows Agent Installation
docs.text: The HitStor agent is a lightweight binary that sends encrypted, deduplicated backups from a Windows machine to a remote HitStor server over gRPC. The NSIS installer registers the agent as a Windows Service (selected by default) that is then managed from the HitStor dashboard.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Windows 10 (1809+) or Windows Server 2016+
  • Architecture: amd64 (the installer is amd64 only; an arm64 binary can be built from source with make agent-windows-arm64)
  • Network access to the HitStor server (default port 8420), and from the server to the agent's listen port (default 8422)
  • Administrator privileges (required for installation and service management)

docs.title: Download
docs.text:
Download the agent installer from the GitHub Releases page:

  • hitstor-agent-x.y.z-windows-amd64-setup.exe

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
1. Run the installer:

    hitstor-agent-x.y.z-windows-amd64-setup.exe

  2. Accept the license agreement.

  3. Choose the installation directory (default: C:\Program Files\HitStor Agent\).
  4. On the Components page, select the components to install:
    • HitStor Agent (required) -- installs the agent binary and configuration.
    • Install as Windows Service (selected by default) -- registers and starts the agent as a Windows Service, and opens its listen port in Windows Firewall.
  5. On the Agent Configuration page, keep the listen port (default 8422) unless another service uses it. The server connects to this port to register and manage the agent.
  6. Click Install. The last page shows the listen port, the agent token, and the next steps.

The installer performs the following steps:

  • Copies hitstor-agent.exe to the installation directory and adds the directory to the system PATH.
  • Creates %ProgramData%\HitStor\, restricted to SYSTEM and Administrators, with agent-config.yaml.example, agent.env (HITSTOR_AGENT_LISTEN_PORT), and an agent-config.yaml without backup paths (an existing one is preserved). On upgrade, the credentials in agent.env are kept.
  • Creates a Start Menu shortcut for the uninstaller.
  • If the service component is selected, registers the HitStorAgent Windows Service with --config %ProgramData%\HitStor\agent-config.yaml, adds the firewall rule HitStor Agent for the listen port, and starts the service. The service generates the agent token (%ProgramData%\HitStor\agent-token) on first start.

docs.title: Register the Agent
docs.text: In the HitStor dashboard, go to Agents → Add Agent and enter this machine's IP address, the listen port, and the agent token shown at the end of the installation (hitstor-agent show-id prints it again from an elevated prompt). The server sends the agent its address and API key, which the agent stores in agent.env. Then create backup jobs under Backups; backup paths and schedules are managed from the dashboard.

docs.title: Manual Configuration
docs.text:
A dashboard-managed agent needs no configuration file edits. To run the agent CLI against a server without dashboard registration (for example with an API key from hitstor serve agent add <name>), use a configuration file. The service reads %ProgramData%\HitStor\agent-config.yaml (passed with --config) and %ProgramData%\HitStor\agent.env; CLI commands read %AppData%\hitstor\config.yaml unless you pass --config.

Edit the system-wide file (agent-config.yaml.example in the same folder lists every option):

notepad "$env:ProgramData\HitStor\agent-config.yaml"

docs.title: Required Settings
docs.text:
At minimum, configure the server address and API key:

agent_server: "backup-server.internal:8420"
agent_api_key: "your-64-char-hex-api-key"

docs.title: Full Example
docs.text:
agent_server: "backup-server.internal:8420"
agent_api_key: "your-64-char-hex-api-key"
agent_ca_cert: "C:\\certs\\ca.crt"
agent_hostname: "win-workstation-01"
agent_paths:
  - "C:\\Users"
  - "C:\\Data"
agent_excludes:
  - "*.tmp"
  - "Thumbs.db"
  - "desktop.ini"

docs.title: Verify the Installation
docs.text:
Open a new elevated PowerShell window and run:

Get-Service HitStorAgent
hitstor-agent show-id

Test connectivity to the server:

hitstor-agent ping --server backup-server.internal:8420 --ca-cert C:\certs\ca.crt

docs.title: Running a Manual Backup
docs.text:
hitstor-agent backup C:\Users C:\Data

Or with explicit flags:

hitstor-agent backup --server backup-server:8420 --api-key <key> --ca-cert ca.crt C:\Users C:\Data

docs.title: Windows Service Management
docs.text: The agent can run as a Windows Service for unattended scheduled backups. Administrator privileges are required for all service operations.

docs.title: Install the Service
docs.text:
If you did not select the service component during installation, you can install it manually:

hitstor-agent service install --config "$env:ProgramData\HitStor\agent-config.yaml"

Options:

Flag Default Description --name HitStorAgent Windows Service name --display HitStor Backup Agent Display name in the Services console --config (none) Configuration file the service is started with; without it the service account's default (%AppData%\hitstor\config.yaml) is used

--server, --api-key, and --ca-cert given to service install are also passed to the service.

docs.title: Start and Stop
docs.text:
hitstor-agent service start
hitstor-agent service stop

You can also manage the service through the Windows Services console (services.msc).

docs.title: Uninstall the Service
docs.text:
hitstor-agent service stop
hitstor-agent service uninstall

docs.title: Service Behavior
docs.text: When running as a service, the agent runs in daemon mode: it listens on the listen port (HITSTOR_AGENT_LISTEN_PORT in agent.env, default 8422) for the server, and polls the server every 5 minutes for its backup jobs, which run on the schedules set in the dashboard. It reads agent.env from %ProgramData%\HitStor\ and logs to %ProgramData%\HitStor\logs\agent.log.

docs.title: Known Limitations
docs.text: Area Limitation UID / GID Always stored as 0. Windows has no Unix ownership model. File mode Simplified: 0666 for normal files, 0444 for read-only. Not Unix permissions. CTime Represents file creation time on Windows (not change time as on Unix). Symlinks Require Developer Mode or admin privileges. Skipped if unavailable. NTFS Alternate Data Streams Not backed up. Windows ACLs Not backed up. Permissions are not preserved during restore. Long paths (>260 chars) Supported via Go 1.24 long path handling.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
Use Add/Remove Programs in Windows Settings, or run the uninstaller directly:

& "$env:ProgramFiles\HitStor Agent\uninstall.exe"

The uninstaller stops and removes the Windows Service (if installed) and the HitStor Agent firewall rule, removes the binary, PATH entry, Start Menu shortcuts, and registry entries, and deletes the agent's files in %ProgramData%\HitStor\ (agent.env, agent-config.yaml, the agent token, and its certificates). Register the agent again after a reinstall.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Getting Started -- learn the full backup lifecycle.
  • Configuration -- config file schema and environment variables.

docs.title: Windows Server Installation
docs.text: HitStor provides an NSIS installer for deploying the backup server on Windows. The installer adds hitstor.exe to the system PATH, creates the configuration directory, registers HitStor as a Windows Service, and registers an uninstaller in Add/Remove Programs.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Windows 10 (1809+) or Windows Server 2016+
  • Architecture: amd64
  • Administrator privileges (required for installation)

docs.title: Download
docs.text:
Download the server installer from the GitHub Releases page:

  • hitstor-x.y.z-windows-amd64-setup.exe

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
1. Run the installer:

    hitstor-x.y.z-windows-amd64-setup.exe

  2. Accept the license agreement.

  3. Choose the installation directory (default: C:\Program Files\HitStor\).
  4. Choose the components (both selected by default):
    • Windows Firewall rules -- allow inbound TCP 8420 (agents) and 8421 (dashboard) for hitstor.exe.
    • Install as Windows Service -- register and start the HitStor service.
  5. Click Install.

The installer performs the following steps:

  • Stops the HitStor service if it is already installed (upgrade).
  • Copies hitstor.exe to the installation directory and adds it to the system PATH.
  • Creates %ProgramData%\HitStor\, restricted to Administrators and SYSTEM, with config.yaml.example.
  • Creates %ProgramData%\HitStor\config.yaml from the example if it does not exist (an existing one is preserved).
  • Registers the HitStor Windows Service, which runs hitstor serve --config %ProgramData%\HitStor\config.yaml as LocalSystem with automatic start, and starts it.
  • Registers the application in Add/Remove Programs.

docs.title: Unattended install and upgrade
docs.text:
Run the installer with /S from an elevated prompt. All components are installed, and running the same command with a newer installer upgrades in place (the service is stopped, the binary replaced, and the service re-registered and started):

.\hitstor-x.y.z-windows-amd64-setup.exe /S

docs.title: Verify the Installation
docs.text:
Open a new PowerShell or Command Prompt window (required so the updated PATH takes effect) and run:

hitstor version
Get-Service HitStor

hitstor version prints the version, commit hash, and build date.

docs.title: First Login
docs.text:
With no repositories configured, the server starts in setup mode (dashboard only) and serves it over plain HTTP. Open http://<server>:8421. HTTPS (self-signed by default) is enabled once a repository is configured and the service restarts.

There is no default dashboard password. If config.yaml has none, the server generates one on first start, saves its hash to config.yaml, and logs the plaintext once to %ProgramData%\HitStor\logs\server.log. Read it on the server from an elevated PowerShell:

Select-String -Path "$env:ProgramData\HitStor\logs\server.log" -Pattern "generated one" |
  Select-Object -Last 1 |
  ForEach-Object { ($_.Line | ConvertFrom-Json).fields.password }

Sign in with it and create a repository from the Storage page, then restart the service (Restart-Service HitStor). Open https://<server>:8421: the dashboard now asks you to Create the first administrator. Enter the same password, choose the administrator's user name and password, and set up an authenticator app. From then on everyone signs in with a personal account and the generated password no longer signs in. See Dashboard Password and First Administrator, which also covers resetting a lost password and creating the administrator from the console with hitstor serve user add.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Edit %ProgramData%\HitStor\config.yaml (see config.yaml.example in the same folder for all options) and restart the service:

notepad "$env:ProgramData\HitStor\config.yaml"
Restart-Service HitStor

docs.title: Managing the Service
docs.text:
The installer manages the service for you. To do it by hand (elevated prompt):

hitstor service install --config "$env:ProgramData\HitStor\config.yaml"
hitstor service start
hitstor service stop
hitstor service uninstall

All subcommands accept --name (default HitStor). You can also use Start-Service/Stop-Service HitStor or the Services console. The service writes to %ProgramData%\HitStor\logs\server.log.

To run the server in the foreground instead (for troubleshooting), stop the service and run:

hitstor serve --config "$env:ProgramData\HitStor\config.yaml"

docs.title: Firewall Configuration
docs.text:
The Windows Firewall rules component creates the rules HitStor Server gRPC (8420) and HitStor Server Dashboard (8421), open to any remote address. To restrict them, for example to an admin network:

Set-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "HitStor Server Dashboard" -RemoteAddress 10.0.0.0/24

If you skipped that component, create the rules yourself:

New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "HitStor gRPC" -Direction Inbound -LocalPort 8420 -Protocol TCP -Action Allow
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "HitStor Dashboard" -Direction Inbound -LocalPort 8421 -Protocol TCP -Action Allow

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
Use Add/Remove Programs in Windows Settings, or run the uninstaller directly:

& "$env:ProgramFiles\HitStor\uninstall.exe"

The uninstaller stops and removes the service and firewall rules, and removes the binary, PATH entry, Start Menu shortcuts, and registry entries. Configuration files in %ProgramData%\HitStor\ and repository data are not deleted.

docs.title: Configuration Reference
docs.text: Complete reference for all HitStor configuration keys. Configuration is stored in YAML format. Without --config, HitStor uses /etc/hitstor/config.yaml when it exists and is readable, and otherwise ~/.config/hitstor/config.yaml (%AppData%\hitstor\config.yaml on Windows). The Windows server service uses %ProgramData%\HitStor\config.yaml.

docs.title: Precedence
docs.text:
Values are resolved in this order (highest priority first):

  1. CLI flag -- --repo /path
  2. Config file -- repo: /path
  3. Environment variable -- HITSTOR_REPO=/path (used only when neither a flag nor the config file sets the value)
  4. Default value

docs.title: Core Settings
docs.text: Key Type Default CLI Flag Env Var Description repo string --repo HITSTOR_REPO Repository location (local path, s3:endpoint/bucket, or plugin:name/args) password_file string --password-file Path to file containing the repository password parallel int 0 --parallel Number of parallel workers (0 = auto-detect based on CPU count) exclude list Global exclude patterns (applied to all backups) sync_writes bool false HITSTOR_SYNC_WRITES=1 Fsync local repository files after each atomic rename (durability over speed) min_free_reserve_bytes int 1073741824 (1 GiB) Minimum free disk space required before writing pack files to a local repository

docs.title: S3 Backend
docs.text: Key Type Default CLI Flag Description s3_access_key string --s3-access-key S3 access key (sensitive -- masked in config show) s3_secret_key string --s3-secret-key S3 secret key (sensitive -- masked in config show) s3_region string us-east-1 --s3-region S3 region

docs.title: Server Settings
docs.text:
Used by hitstor serve to configure the gRPC server and web dashboard.

Key Type Default CLI Flag Description serve_port int 8420 --port gRPC server listen port serve_tls_cert string --tls-cert Path to TLS certificate file serve_tls_key string --tls-key Path to TLS private key file serve_dashboard_port int 8421 --dashboard-port HTTP dashboard listen port serve_dashboard_password string Dashboard setup password (sensitive). It signs in while the server has no repository and is asked for once to create the first administrator; after that, people sign in with their own accounts. If empty, a random one is generated at startup and logged once; see Dashboard Password and First Administrator serve_dashboard_language string Default dashboard language code (en, es). Empty uses the browser language; users can still switch with the selector. See Translations serve_advertise_addr string --advertise-addr Address advertised to agents for registration (use when server is behind NAT) update_check bool false Enable automatic version checks. When enabled, the server checks for updates every 24 hours and shows a banner in the dashboard. Can also be turned on under Settings → General. update_url string Custom update check URL (empty = GitHub Releases API)

docs.title: Alerting
docs.text: Key Type Default Description alert_webhook_url string Webhook URL for alert notifications (receives POST with JSON payload) alert_stale_threshold int 25 Hours before an agent is considered stale (minimum: 1) alert_notifier_plugins list Notifier plugin names to load for alert delivery

docs.title: Agent Settings
docs.text:
Used by hitstor-agent to configure the remote backup agent.

Key Type Default CLI Flag Env Var Description agent_server string --server HITSTOR_AGENT_SERVER Remote server address (host:port) agent_api_key string --api-key HITSTOR_AGENT_API_KEY Agent API key for authentication (sensitive -- 64-char hex) agent_ca_cert string --ca-cert Path to CA certificate for TLS verification agent_hostname string backup --host Override hostname sent to server (defaults to system hostname) agent_paths list Default backup paths (used when no paths given on command line) agent_excludes list Default exclude patterns for agent backups

docs.title: Plugin Settings
docs.text: Key Type Default Description plugin_dir string Directory to search for plugin binaries (searched before $PATH) hook_plugins list Hook plugin names to load for pre/post-backup lifecycle events fs_scanner_plugin string Filesystem scanner plugin name (builtin or a custom Scanner plugin; only one active at a time) plugin_store_dir string /var/lib/hitstor/plugins (Linux), C:\ProgramData\HitStor\plugins (Windows) Agent: directory where workload plugin packages are installed plugin_trusted_keys list Agent: extra base64 ed25519 public keys trusted to sign plugin packages, in addition to the official HitStor key plugin_allow_unsigned bool false Agent: accept unsigned plugin packages. Development only; packages signed by an untrusted key are still rejected

docs.title: Integrations (integrations)
docs.text:
Used by Sentinel (Gemini). Sensitive values are stored encrypted (AES-256-GCM, base64) using the repository encryption key. Editable from the dashboard Settings → Integrations tab.

Key Type Description gemini_api_key_encrypted string Encrypted Gemini API key for Sentinel (and GEMINI_API_KEY env export) gemini_model string Gemini model (default: gemini-1.5-pro)

GEMINI_API_KEY still works and takes precedence when set. Use Import from environment in Settings to migrate it to encrypted YAML.

docs.title: Ignored legacy keys
docs.text: Microsoft 365 (m365_*), cloud provider (gcp_project, aws_role_arn, aws_region, azure_tenant, azure_client, azure_sub), and collector_plugins keys were removed from the config schema in an earlier release. Existing config.yaml files containing them still load — YAML silently ignores unknown keys — but the values are never read. Remove these keys at your convenience.

docs.title: Email (email)
docs.text:
The outgoing mail server for account emails: invitations to new users and password reset links. Secrets are stored encrypted with the repository key. Editable from the dashboard Settings → Email tab; see Users and access.

Key Type Description host string SMTP server. Empty turns account emails off port int Port (default: 587 for starttls, 465 for tls, 25 for none) security string starttls, tls or none (plain SMTP, for a relay on a trusted network) auth string none (the server accepts mail by client address), password or microsoft365 (OAuth 2.0 app) username string password: user name. microsoft365: mailbox to sign in as, if not from password_encrypted string password: encrypted password tenant_id string microsoft365: directory (tenant) ID client_id string microsoft365: application (client) ID client_secret_encrypted string microsoft365: encrypted client secret from string Sender address from_name string Sender name tls_skip_verify bool Accept any server certificate (self-signed relays only) dashboard_url string The dashboard's address as people reach it, the base of the links in emails

docs.title: Reports (reports)
docs.text:
The reports emailed on a schedule, a list. Editable from Administration → Reports; see Reports.

Key Type Description id string Identifier name string Name shown in the list and the email subject type string summary (protection summary) or daily (daily backup status) period string summary: week or month (last 7 or 30 days) cron string When to send it (cron expression) timezone string Time zone of the schedule and of the dates in the report recipients list Email addresses agents list Agents covered; empty: every agent language string en or es; empty: the dashboard's default enabled bool Send it on schedule created, last_sent, last_error Kept by the server

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
Server and agent log retention: the in-memory buffer behind the dashboard's Logs page and the rotated log file. Each key has an environment variable that overrides it.

Key Type Default Env Var Description log_max_entries int 5000 HITSTOR_LOG_MAX_ENTRIES Entries kept in memory (500-50000) log_file_enabled bool true HITSTOR_LOG_FILE_ENABLED Write the log file log_file_path string /var/log/hitstor/server.log (C:\ProgramData\HitStor\logs\server.log on Windows); the agent writes agent.log in the same folder HITSTOR_LOG_FILE_PATH Log file path log_rotate_max_mb int 50 HITSTOR_LOG_ROTATE_MAX_MB Rotate the file at this size (at most 500) log_rotate_max_files int 5 HITSTOR_LOG_ROTATE_MAX_FILES Rotated files kept (at most 20)

docs.title: Sentinel (sentinel)
docs.text: Optional Sentinel telemetry settings (future dashboard editing). Keys mirror HITSTOR_SENTINEL_* environment variables.

docs.title: Multi-Repository (repositories)
docs.text:
When running hitstor serve with multiple repositories, define a list instead of a single repo:

repositories:
  - name: production
    type: local
    path: /var/lib/hitstor/prod-repo
    password_file: /etc/hitstor/prod-password

  - name: offsite
    type: s3
    endpoint: s3.amazonaws.com
    bucket: company-backups
    region: us-east-1
    access_key_encrypted: <base64 AES-256-GCM ciphertext>
    secret_key_encrypted: <base64 AES-256-GCM ciphertext>
    password_file: /etc/hitstor/s3-repo-password

S3 credentials are stored encrypted in the config file. The dashboard Storage page can create repositories without hand-editing ciphertext.

If repositories is empty and repo is set, the server runs in single-repository legacy mode.

docs.title: Key Types
docs.text: Type Description Management Commands string Single value config set, config unset int Integer value config set, config unset list Ordered list of values config add, config remove

docs.title: Local Server
docs.text:
repo: /var/lib/hitstor/repo
parallel: 4
exclude:
  - "*.tmp"
  - ".cache"
serve_port: 8420
serve_tls_cert: /etc/hitstor/tls/cert.pem
serve_tls_key: /etc/hitstor/tls/key.pem
serve_dashboard_port: 8421
alert_webhook_url: https://hooks.slack.com/services/T.../B.../xxx
alert_stale_threshold: 25

docs.title: Remote Agent
docs.text:
agent_server: backup.internal:8420
agent_api_key: a1b2c3d4e5f6...  # 64-char hex
agent_ca_cert: /etc/hitstor/ca.pem
agent_paths:
  - /etc
  - /home
  - /var/lib
agent_excludes:
  - "*.log"
  - ".cache"

docs.text:
repo: s3:https://s3.amazonaws.com/my-backup-bucket
s3_access_key: AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE
s3_secret_key: wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY
s3_region: us-west-2

docs.title: Dashboard HTTP API
docs.text:
The embedded dashboard served by hitstor serve exposes a JSON API on the HTTP port (default 8421). Routes are defined in internal/dashboard/dashboard.go.

Unless noted, endpoints require a signed-in session (see Authentication), and each route needs a role: reads need the viewer role, changes to jobs the backup operator role, restores the restore operator role, and users, storage, settings, and other server-wide changes the administrator. Routes about one agent accept a role on that agent; routes that span agents need the role on every agent. Sensitive changes also need a recent sign-in. See Users and Access.

docs.title: Pages
docs.text:
Path Description GET / Overview GET /backups Backup jobs list GET /backups/{id} Backup job detail GET /agents Agents GET /agents/{name} Agent detail GET /snapshots/{id} Snapshot detail (browse + restore) GET /storage Repository management GET /storage/{name} Repository detail GET /restores Restore sessions GET /settings Server settings (General, Security/TLS, Network, Integrations, Notifications, Email, Plugins) GET /disaster Disaster recovery GET /logs Server and agent logs GET /reports Scheduled reports GET /users, GET /users/{name} Users and access (administrators) GET /audit Audit log (administrators) GET /account, GET /account/password The signed-in user's account and password change

GET /snapshots redirects to /storage.

docs.title: Repositories & Storage
docs.text: Method Path Description GET /api/repos List repositories POST /api/repos Create repository (local or S3) DELETE /api/repos/{name} Disconnect repository GET /api/disk-space?path= Disk space for a path POST /api/repos/test-s3 Test S3 credentials POST /api/repos/detect Detect existing repo at path GET /api/repos/{name}/growth Growth chart data (?range=, ?granularity=) POST /api/repos/{name}/check Start integrity check POST /api/repos/{name}/prune Start prune GET /api/repos/{name}/sessions Active sessions for repo GET /api/repos/{name}, /api/repos/{name}/health, /api/repos/{name}/snapshots One repository's metrics, operational health, and snapshots grouped by agent GET /api/repos/growth Growth data for several repositories in one request POST /api/repos/{name}/forget Apply a retention policy (administrators, recent sign-in) POST /api/repos/detect-s3, /api/repos/validate-path Detect an existing repository in a bucket; validate a local path

docs.title: Snapshots & Restore
docs.text: Method Path Description GET /api/snapshots?host=&limit= List snapshots (newest first) GET /api/snapshots/{id}/tree?path= Browse snapshot file tree POST /api/snapshots/{id}/restore Start agent restore (agent_name, target_path, optional includes) GET /api/restores List restore sessions GET /api/restores/sources Sources that can be restored, as listed on the Restores page GET /api/restore/{id}/events SSE restore progress GET /api/agents/{name}/plugins/{plugin}/browse?path= List the objects a workload plugin on the agent can back up, with detail, status, and whether each takes object settings (configurable) and has them saved (configured) GET /api/agents/{name}/plugins/{plugin}/object-config?path= Settings saved on the agent for one object (configured, values without passwords, secrets_set) PUT /api/agents/{name}/plugins/{plugin}/object-config Test and save an object's settings on the agent (path, values; an empty password keeps the saved one), or remove them (path, remove: true). The server stores nothing GET /api/workload/points?agent=&plugin=&object= Items available to restore a workload object, oldest first GET /api/workload/catalog?agent=&plugin=&snapshot= Every item a plugin backed up on an agent, newest first, with its object; snapshot (an ID prefix) keeps one snapshot's POST /api/workload/restore-plan Preview a workload restore without running it (same body as POST /api/workload/restores): the items it applies, the files it writes (key, kind, source, target), warnings, and a summary POST /api/workload/restores Start a workload restore (agent_name, plugin, object; optional source_agent to restore another agent's backups, target time, options, plugin_settings) GET /api/workload/restores/{id} Workload restore status: plan, bytes sent, result GET /api/plugin-packages List uploaded plugin packages POST /api/plugin-packages Upload a plugin package (the .hpk file as an application/octet-stream body); rejected unless signed by a trusted key DELETE /api/plugin-packages/{file} Delete an uploaded package POST /api/agents/{name}/plugins Install an uploaded package on a managed agent (package, optional upgrade, allow_downgrade); the agent verifies it again DELETE /api/agents/{name}/plugins/{id} Uninstall a plugin from a managed agent; refused while a job uses it

docs.text: Method Path Description GET /api/stats Repository statistics GET /api/active-backups Active backup sessions GET /api/backup-progress/events SSE backup progress (all sessions) GET /api/operations/{id}/events SSE for check/prune operations

docs.text: Method Path Description GET /api/settings Effective server settings (secrets masked) PUT /api/settings/general update_check, update_url, parallel, sync_writes, min_free_reserve_bytes PUT /api/settings/security dashboard_password (empty = keep current); may set restart_required PUT /api/settings/network serve_port, serve_dashboard_port, serve_advertise_addr; may set restart_required PUT /api/settings/notifications alert_webhook_url, alert_stale_threshold, alert_notifier_plugins PUT /api/settings/email Outgoing mail server for invitations, password reset links, and reports (recent sign-in) POST /api/settings/email/test Send a test email with the settings in the request PUT /api/settings/integrations Gemini key/model (gemini_api_key empty = keep current) POST /api/settings/integrations/import-env Migrate GEMINI_API_KEY into encrypted YAML GET /api/settings/tls/status TLS certificate metadata (source, expiry, SANs) POST /api/settings/tls/upload Multipart cert + key PEM files; sets restart_required POST /api/settings/test/gemini Validate Gemini API key POST /api/settings/test/webhook POST test payload to configured webhook URL

docs.title: Users, Account, and Audit
docs.text:
Method Path Description GET /api/users List users (administrators) POST /api/users Create a user: sends an invitation when email is set up, otherwise returns a temporary password GET / PUT / DELETE /api/users/{name} Read, change (roles, status, profile), or delete a user POST /api/users/{name}/password Reset a user's password (temporary password, or a reset link by email) DELETE /api/users/{name}/second-factor Reset a user's two-step verification GET /api/users/{name}/sessions A user's sessions DELETE /api/users/{name}/sessions/{id} End one of a user's sessions POST /api/account/password Change the signed-in user's password POST /api/account/recovery-codes Generate new recovery codes (recent sign-in) PUT /api/account/profile Change the signed-in user's display name GET / DELETE /api/account/sessions List the signed-in user's sessions, or end all but the current one DELETE /api/account/sessions/{id} End one of the signed-in user's sessions POST /api/reauth Confirm the password and a code before a sensitive action GET /api/session Remaining session time (does not count as activity) POST /api/session/activity Record user activity so the session stays open GET /api/audit, /api/audit/export Audit log, and its CSV export (administrators)

All user changes require an administrator and a recent sign-in.

docs.text:
Method Path Description GET /api/reports List scheduled reports POST /api/reports Create a scheduled report PUT / DELETE /api/reports/{id} Change or delete a report POST /api/reports/{id}/send Send a report now GET /api/reports/pdf Download a report as PDF, as it would be sent now

Reports are for administrators. See Reports.

docs.title: Disaster Recovery and Bare Metal
docs.text:
Method Path Description GET /api/disaster/plans, /api/disaster/plans/{agent} Recovery readiness of every system, or one system's plan POST /api/disaster/recover Start a full-system recovery (administrators, recent sign-in) GET /api/disaster/recoveries, /api/disaster/recoveries/{id} Orchestrated recoveries and their status GET /api/bmr/hosts Agents with their recovery-media status POST /api/bmr/media/{agent}/build Build recovery media on an agent GET / DELETE /api/bmr/media/{agent}/download, /api/bmr/media/{agent} Download or discard a host's cached recovery image POST /api/bmr/prepare/{agent} Issue a single-use recovery token (administrators, recent sign-in) GET / DELETE /api/bmr/tokens, /api/bmr/tokens/{id} List unused recovery tokens, or revoke one

See Disaster Recovery and Bare-metal restore.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text: Method Path Description GET /api/logs Server and agent log entries GET /api/logs/export Export log entries

docs.title: Alerts (Sentinel)
docs.text: Method Path Description GET /api/alerts List sentinel/security alerts POST /api/alerts/{id}/resolve Resolve alert

docs.title: Metrics (unauthenticated)
docs.text: Method Path Description GET /metrics Prometheus text exposition

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Method Path Description GET / POST /login Sign-in page; submit user name and password (or, before any account exists, the dashboard password) GET / POST /login/code Second step: a code from the authenticator app, or a recovery code GET / POST /login/enroll Set up the authenticator at the first sign-in GET / POST /login/forgot Request a password reset link by email GET / POST /login/reset Choose a new password from an emailed link GET / POST /setup Create the first administrator with the dashboard password POST /logout End session

The session is the hitstor_session cookie, issued only after both sign-in steps. There are no API tokens: scripts call the API with the cookie of a signed-in user, and the session ends after the inactivity timeout like any other (see Sessions and lockout). A request that needs a recent sign-in answers 403 with {"error": "reauth_required"} and the header X-HitStor-Reauth: 1; confirm with POST /api/reauth and retry. State-changing requests sent by a browser from another origin are rejected.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: HitStor reads the following environment variables. CLI flags take precedence over them. For the repository location and the agent's server, API key, and CA certificate, a value in the config file also takes precedence: the environment variable is only used when neither a flag nor the config file sets it. The HITSTOR_LOG_* variables override their config keys.

docs.title: Server (hitstor)
docs.text: Variable Config Key Description HITSTOR_REPO repo Repository location (local path, s3:endpoint/bucket, or plugin:name/args) HITSTOR_PASSWORD -- Repository password (no config key). Used when --password is not given; takes precedence over --password-file HITSTOR_SYNC_WRITES sync_writes 1 fsyncs local repository files after each atomic rename HITSTOR_LOG_MAX_ENTRIES, HITSTOR_LOG_FILE_ENABLED, HITSTOR_LOG_FILE_PATH, HITSTOR_LOG_ROTATE_MAX_MB, HITSTOR_LOG_ROTATE_MAX_FILES log_* Log retention and rotation (also read by the agent); see Configuration Reference PORT -- When set, hitstor serve serves gRPC and the dashboard together on this single port (for platforms that expose one port per container)

docs.title: Docker image and Linux installer
docs.text:
These are read by the container entrypoint or the .run installer, not by the hitstor binary:

Variable Read by Description HITSTOR_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD Docker entrypoint, server .run --no-wizard Dashboard setup password, written to serve_dashboard_password HITSTOR_AUTO_INIT Docker entrypoint false skips the automatic hitstor init of HITSTOR_REPO (default true) HITSTOR_DATA_DIR, HITSTOR_GRPC_PORT, HITSTOR_DASHBOARD_PORT, HITSTOR_ADVERTISE_ADDR Server .run --no-wizard Data directory, ports, and advertise address; see Linux Quick Install

docs.title: Agent (hitstor-agent)
docs.text:
